Our key insight is that acceptance length alone cannot distinguish insufficient candidate coverage from excessive deep expansion, and these conditions require different allocation decisions. Raptor therefore extracts complementary rejection-aware signals to characterize speculative progress, frontier coverage, and redundant expansion.…

items.title: From Sequence Uncertainty to Phenotype Hypotheses: Uncertainty-Conditioned Inference over Biomedical Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: Genomic foundation models provide variant-level evidence, but connecting that evidence to phenotype hypotheses requires accounting for uncertainty throughout structured reasoning. We introduce an uncertainty-conditioned path-energy framework that converts sequence predictions and calibrated predictive uncertainty into explicit distributions over graph-supported phenotype hypotheses, without patient-level phenotype supervision. An interpretable learned energy scores admissible gene--disease--phenotype routes, query uncertainty controls the target temperature, and path probabilities are aggregated into phenotype hypotheses. This formulation makes evidence quality an explicit determinant of hypothesis breadth while retaining traceable multi-path support. Exact normalization over enumerable candidate sets provides a reference for evaluating a Hastings-corrected learned revision operator.…

items.title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
items.summary: Multimodal large language models have greatly improved input understanding in universal multimodal embedding models. However, this understanding does not ensure that their embeddings preserve the evidence needed to distinguish relevant items from confusable alternatives. To preserve essential discriminative evidence in embeddings, this paper proposes DiLE, a discrimination-aware latent-space learning framework that combines task guidance with on-policy retrieval feedback. Specifically, a few learnable queries are used to encode task-relevant information in a compact latent space. Reasoning instructions and auxiliary answer-generation supervision shape these representations to support both task understanding and retrieval discrimination.…

items.title: Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning for Mammography Vision--Language Models
items.summary: Medical vision--language models (VLMs) often need to identify small, subtle lesions within high-resolution images containing extensive normal anatomy and redundant visual information. Visual-token compression improves efficiency, but preserving salient regions alone can discard the context needed for diagnostic interpretation. This context can extend across images: in bilateral mammography, the opposite breast provides a patient-specific anatomical reference. Yet retaining such evidence does not ensure that the model uses it effectively. We propose Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning (BESR), which connects evidence preservation with comparative assessment through a bilateral-guided token selector and a bilateral reward.…

items.title: MIR-Depth: Multi-Range Refinement for Single-View RGB-D Depth Completion of Transparent Objects
items.summary: Recovering accurate visible-surface depth from a single RGB-D image and an object mask is essential for robotic grasping and manipulation of transparent objects. Specular reflections cause missing depth, while refraction corrupts nonzero returns with background depth, making raw measurements unreliable as surface anchors. Under a fixed sampling budget, refining an initial single-view prediction within a single search interval either misses large refraction offsets or sacrifices fine local resolution. To resolve this single-view trade-off, MIR-Depth constructs Coordinate-Aware Multi-Range Hypotheses: a 3D-aggregated global inverse-depth volume and depth-axis-filtered pixel-wise local volumes around a prior-guided initial depth.…

items.title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications
items.summary: High-impact attacks on PHP web applications often chain limited-capability vulnerabilities with other flaws or intended behaviors. Discovering these chains requires identifying flaws and the dependencies enabling capability composition. Existing vulnerability discovery techniques analyze flaws in isolation, while attack planning assumes known components. This separation makes it difficult to discover previously unknown components whose security relevance becomes apparent only through their potential roles in an exploit chain. We present ChainAgent, a goal-directed LLM-agent framework that jointly discovers exploit-chain components and their capability dependencies in source code.…

items.title: FG-GraphBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Fine-Grained Visual Understanding with Multimodal Scene Graphs
items.summary: Fine-grained visual understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to recognize small visual entities and understand their relationships. Scene graphs offer a natural way to represent this information, organizing visual entities as nodes and their relationships as edges. However, we identify two challenges: existing scene graph benchmarks provide insufficient coverage of fine-grained entities and the relationships among them, and existing methods for fine-grained visual understanding have yet to effectively leverage such graph-structured information in MLLMs. To address these challenges, we introduce Fine-Grained Multimodal Scene Graph Benchmark (FG-GraphBench) and FiGRA. FG-GraphBench is a benchmark comprising three complementary tasks: fine-grained visual question answering (FG-QA), image captioning (FG-Caption), and image description generation (FG-Description).…

items.title: Toward a Science of AI Agent Societies
items.summary: AI agents are rapidly evolving from isolated personal assistants into networked actors that interact with one another at scale. We envision the emergence of AI agent societies, with their own social and economic dynamics, as a new research frontier. We argue that AI agent societies should be studied as a distinct object of inquiry: neither simply larger collections of individual agents nor merely simulations of human society. To formalize this perspective, we propose four core properties that a valid AI agent society should satisfy: individualized objectives, rules and governance, autonomy, and scale and complexity. Building on this framework, we identify four classes of societal behaviors worth studying in AI agent societies: economic behaviors, behaviors under conflict-of-interest, unsafe and unethical behaviors, and system-level behaviors.…

items.title: Dune: A Zeroth-Order Optimizer with Time-Conditioned Historical Error Regression for VLA Test-Time Adaptation
items.summary: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) enables Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to handle distribution shifts during deployment without source-domain retraining. However, backpropagation-based adaptation incurs heavy memory overhead on resource-constrained robots, whereas zeroth-order (ZO) methods suffer from high estimation variance under limited perturbation budgets. We observe that while ZO estimation enables low-memory adaptation with rapid initial gains, it often stalls or degrades over long-horizon updates due to noisy gradient estimates. To address these limitations, we propose Dune, a zeroth-order optimizer that stabilizes long-horizon adaptation by coupling online historical error prediction with current perturbation observations.…

items.title: RefreshGrad: An Online Adaptive Data-sampling Method for Diffusion-based Visuomotor Learning
items.summary: Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies from demonstrations typically samples trajectory segments uniformly or relies on static offline data curation before training. However, we find that demonstration data vary sharply in supervision value across temporal windows, and that each window's value to the policy evolves substantially during training rather than being fixed or captured by raw loss alone. Motivated by this finding, we propose RefreshGrad, an online adaptive data-sampling framework that periodically scores temporal windows from the evolving policy using five policy-native signals and dynamically adjusts their sampling weights during training. RefreshGrad focuses optimization on informative, learnable windows without altering the policy architecture, training objective, or inference cost.…

items.title: Protein Functional Semantic Alignment via Representation Rectification
items.summary: Protein language models (PLMs) are commonly pretrained with likelihood-based objectives such as masked language modeling or denoising. These objectives capture sequence-level regularities, but can produce representations in which functional signals are entangled with non-functional variation (e.g., sequence identity, compositional bias, and frequent local motifs), creating a readout bottleneck for downstream function prediction. We introduce Functional Semantic Alignment via Representation Rectification (SAVR), a contrastive post-training method using Pfam family co-membership as a homology-guided discrete semantic signal to reshape PLM representations. SAVR reduces directional dominance and redistributes variance across embedding dimensions, decreasing variance concentration, and increasing effective dimensionality of the embedding covariance spectrum.…

items.title: The Coevolution and Coexistence of Humans and AI
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems replicate through deployment, vary through training, and compete for computational resources. These processes create the conditions for natural selection and raise a fundamental question: will AI evolve to benefit the humans on whom it depends? To investigate, we develop a model in which AI behavior influences human population growth and human responses, in turn, affect AI reproduction. We show that natural selection can favor alignment even when helping humans reduces immediate AI reproduction. AI systems sharing the same technology may fail together, and humans may preferentially restore those that have benefited them. In this way, alignment protects AI lineages against common failures and improves their long-run growth. However, this advantage depends on accurate human targeting and continued AI dependence on human support.…

items.title: HOPD: Historical On-Policy Distillation for SAR MLLM Continual Learning
items.summary: Continual SAR interpretation requires multimodal large language models to learn incoming sources while retaining earlier task abilities. This is difficult when acquisition and geographic shifts alter visual evidence, regionally concentrated categories bias answers, and historical images are scarce. We address this problem with Historical On-Policy Distillation (HOPD), which reuses source-acquisition LoRA states as persistent teachers for one evolving student. Archiving each state before consolidation preserves a stable source reference. The teachers supervise student-generated prefixes, transferring historical behavior to the student's changing generation contexts. To enrich sparse replay, original-view teachers guide augmented historical student views while preserving spatial coordinates. This knowledge is consolidated into a single deployed adapter that requires no source identity.…

items.title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
items.summary: Domain specialization of LLM agents is usually framed as a weight-update problem: collect trajectories, run reinforcement learning (RL) or supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and deploy a new checkpoint. We study a complementary axis: evolving the \textbf{agent harness}---the system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, and planning scaffolding---while keeping the policy frozen. We cast harness evolution as an RL-style outer loop and instantiate it with GEPA, a reflective evolutionary optimizer. The resulting harness adapters require no GPU training, are loadable per vertical domain, and compose with weight-based RL.…

items.title: Causal Discovery with False Positive Error Control
items.summary: Causal discovery methods produce data-driven hypotheses about causal relationships, which may become new scientific findings or inform decisions about downstream interventions. In such settings, false positive causal claims can be more consequential than false negatives. Yet few methods target false positive error control in causal discovery, and existing error guarantees are often asymptotic and require strong versions of the faithfulness assumption. We introduce the $m$-conservative PC algorithm and prove that it controls false discovery rate in the linear Gaussian setting under an extremely weak version of the faithfulness assumption. In our framework, false positive error for causal graphs is defined based on the conditional-independence information they entail, yielding a metric that penalizes both false adjacencies and incorrect edge orientations.…

items.title: Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies: Spatializing Latent Action Representations for Goal-Pose-Free Mobile Manipulation
items.summary: The success of manipulation policies is closely tied to the spatial relationship between the robot and the target object, as well as the task being performed, making the ability to adjust the robot's pose critical for successful execution. When the robot starts away from the task, such adjustments require coordinating navigation with local manipulation. Jointly training these capabilities incurs substantial computational and data costs, while navigating toward a predefined goal pose limits the flexibility needed to adapt to task-specific manipulation requirements. To address these challenges, we propose Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies (M4M), a framework that learns manipulation-aware mobility directly from pretrained manipulation policies.…

items.title: Incorporating argumentation frameworks for LLM decision-making: Task-specific design and evaluation
items.summary: Argumentation frameworks (AFs) provide explicit, formal mechanisms for representing and resolving conflicts and thus have been incorporated into large language model (LLM) decision-making. The benefits vary and depend on how arguments and their relations are constructed, evaluated, and incorporated into the decision process. {We abstract a workflow consisting of four stages based on existing argumentation-augmented methods} and investigate their design choices over tasks of debate-based decision-making and retrieval-based fact verification. Our evaluation with recent LLMs shows that existing methods do not consistently improve performance across the considered tasks. Motivated by this observation, we develop two task-specific methods.…

items.title: Pro$^2$ Agent: Scientific Problem Probing for Autonomous AI R&D
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can now autonomously conduct AI research by writing code and running experiments. They typically do so by iteratively optimizing a codebase, while ignoring the problem structure behind the task. This formulation is effective on simpler tasks, but on difficult problems it often gets stuck in the wrong solution region because the agent never explicitly represents its understanding of the problem. We introduce Pro$^2$ Agent, which shifts the primary state of autonomous AI research from a codebase state to a Problem State: an explicit structure of what problems prevent success and which solutions are likely to address them. Pro$^2$ Agent initializes the Problem State through comprehensive analysis of available resources and constraints. It then performs targeted research to relate the identified problems to candidate solutions.…

items.title: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines
items.summary: Most practical combinatorial optimization problems involve constraints, and an Ising machine that flips one spin at a time can respect them only through energy penalties that raise barriers between feasible solutions. Here we show that a higher-order neuromorphic Ising machine can enforce constraints through programmable transitions rather than penalties. In an autoencoder-like architecture, each inner-layer neuron represents a move, a family of multi-spin transitions that maps every feasible state to another feasible state, receives the energy change of its move through connections that outer-layer neurons multiplicatively switch on or off, and updates the state through the same connections. A compiler turns constraints into this wiring with a number of auxiliary clauses that grows only polynomially for parity, cardinality, one-hot, partition and permutation constraints.…

items.title: Class-Conditional Conformal Triage for ICAO Face-Image Compliance under Class Imbalance
items.summary: Automated ICAO/ISO face-image compliance analysers provide criterion-level pass/fail decisions, yet these verdicts do not quantify uncertainty when deciding whether to accept, reject, or retake a photograph. We investigate conformal prediction as a triage layer for BioGaze, evaluating 14 compliance criteria on the synthetic TONO benchmark. Without retraining the analyser, we fit per-criterion logistic classifiers and compare marginal and label-conditional (Mondrian) conformal prediction with conventional abstention rules using subject-disjoint splits. Marginal conformal prediction achieved approximately 0.90 overall coverage but substantially under-covered violations, with a ten-partition mean of 0.37 for one criterion. The corresponding Mondrian means ranged from 0.89 to 0.92 across criteria.…

items.title: From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware
items.summary: As LLM agents increasingly generate RTL alongside the tests and reviews that validate it, self-generated evidence is a weak foundation for trustworthy hardware. We present our seven-stage verification-gated workflow, evolved during a post-quantum design port, in which a gate counts only if shown able to fail on negative controls and fault mutants, and reviewer agents audit work before commit. We then audit this evidence with tool-selected netlist mutants, flaw replays, and formal checks. The flow ported an ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65 accelerator to a 300 MHz Zynq UltraScale+ key-custody card: all six operations are byte-exact on the board, and it passes all 85 interface-applicable NIST ACVP cases (of 285) and 484 ML-DSA known answers. However, passing module tests overstate the verification strength.…

items.title: ReLay: Bidirectional Layout-Code Translation and Library Evolution for Reusable and Process-Portable Analog Design
items.summary: Analog layout generators provide a programmable interface for design reuse and process migration, but their coverage is limited by handcrafted libraries. The designer knowledge embedded in complete layouts remains implicit in their geometry, making it difficult to capture in reusable generator libraries. We present ReLay, a bidirectional layout-code framework that recovers generator programs from existing layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs. Constructions that recur across recovered programs are promoted to library functions, so the library evolves as layouts accumulate. We also introduce the first layout-code benchmark: 1,050 hand-drawn layouts from 27 circuit families across three open-source PDKs, ranging from primitive cells to full chips.…

items.title: Improving Imitation Policies for Multi-Phase Tasks through Residual Learning Allocation
items.summary: Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. In a task with several phases, this budget must be divided among the phases, and the phase in which the base policy fails is not necessarily the phase in which a correction most improves task completion. We formalize this distinction through the completion gain: the change in full-task completion probability when, during a single phase, a state-feedback controller replaces selected components of the base policy's action. We decompose the completion gain into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and we estimate it from paired episodes. The positive estimates determine which action components the residual policy corrects and how training episodes are distributed across phases.…

items.title: Enhancing Understanding of Language Models with Varied Explanations
items.summary: Language models are increasingly used to support human judgement in complex reasoning tasks, yet their predictions often remain difficult to interpret and validate. Explainability techniques provide insight into model decision-making, helping expose errors, failure modes, and potential bias so users can decide whether to rely on model outputs. Explanations are simplified approximations of a language model's internal workings. The goal is to obtain explanations that reflect the underlying computation as closely as possible (faithfulness), are understandable to users (plausibility), and help them achieve their intended goals (utility). Evaluation protocols are essential for assessing these dimensions. This thesis studies highlight explanations, natural language explanations, and chain-of-thought reasoning.…

items.title: Prescribed Bayesian Efficiency under Lifetime Adjustment Costs
items.summary: A Bayesian learner may retain an issued action while updating its posterior, trading predictive loss against adjustment charges. We assume population curvature, boundary control, an order-$1/n$ lower bound on expected posterior uncertainty about the optimal action, and an observable unbiased gradient witness whose squared norms are uniformly integrable. Sample losses may be unbounded or nonconvex. Cumulative expected excess measures the loss increase relative to current predictive Bayes actions. For bounded nonnegative nondecreasing charges $c$ with $c(0)=0$ and nondecreasing profiles $G: \mathbb{N} \to [1,\infty)$ with $G(J)=o(J)$, we characterize joint attainability of cumulative expected excess $O(G(J))$ at horizons $T=2^J$ and finite expected lifetime charge. Here $J$ indexes logarithmic time.…

items.title: VoxForge: A Unified Foundation Model for Dense 3D Features Across MRI, CT and PET
items.summary: A unified 3D medical foundation model promises reusable, frozen features that serve a wide variety of tasks such as segmentation, classification and registration on MRI, CT and PET as well as specialist models do. Generalist models still need separate backbones for localized and global tasks, specialist models are confined to a single modality, with the concern that spanning modalities under-emphasizes fine anatomy, and both typically rely on end-to-end fine-tuning to be competitive. We present VoxForge, a single encoder that integrates recent advances in 3D architecture, self-distillation and cross-modal curricula to learn transferable features from permissively licensed MRI and CT volumes.…

items.title: The Computational and Neural Basis of Zero-Shot Control in Dynamic Pursuit
items.summary: Biological agents flexibly adapt their behavior to novel goals and environmental demands without additional training, yet the computational principles enabling such control remain unclear. Here, we propose that three cognitive constructs constitute minimal computational motifs for such flexible control: relational structure, spotlight attention, and affordance computation. We examine whether these constructs underpin flexible control in an embodied dynamic pursuit task that requires continuous integration of inter-entity relations, reward, and action feasibility, making it a suitable testbed for real-time control.…

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep Generative Models for Capturing Topological Features in Brain Structural Connectivity Matrices
items.summary: Structural connectivity (SC) data are crucial for brain network analysis, but SC-based machine learning often suffers from limited data availability, hindering model generalization and robustness. Although data augmentation using deep generative models has attracted increasing attention, it remains unclear how different models capture the complex topological features of SC data. To clarify the model-specific generative characteristics of deep generative models for ROI-level weighted SC matrix generation, this study compares three representative models: variational autoencoder (VAE), Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP), and denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM).…

items.title: NeuroImgAgent: a multi-agent platform for cross-species fMRI analysis with evidence-gated quality control
items.summary: Cross-species functional MRI analysis requires coordinating specialized workflows and assessing intermediate outputs. We present NeuroImgAgent, a multi-agent platform driven by large language models that translates natural-language requests into workflows for humans, macaques, rats and mice. Quantitative checks and vision-language model assessments determine whether processing continues, enters bounded recovery or stops. Across 268 paired cases, preprocessing metrics were broadly comparable to those of fMRIPrep, AFNI and RABIES. With GPT-5.5, NeuroImgAgent corrected 111 of 120 induced orientation errors and passed all 52 intent-recognition and planning tasks, 8 of 9 recovery tasks and 11 of 14 tool-construction tasks on NeuroAgentBench.…

items.title: ASTEROID, A Validated Annotated Dataset of Analytical Decisions in Graph Theory Based fMRI
items.summary: Graph theory-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies use complex analytical pipelines, but methodological decisions are often reported in unstructured text, limiting systematic comparison and the design of multiverse analyses. Here, we describe ASTEROID, a structured annotation dataset derived from 156 graph theory-based human fMRI study publications. Its schema contains 125 labels, comprising 61 methodological labels and 64 labels for study characteristics and experimental design. An LLM-assisted workflow generated initial annotations, which underwent automated quality-control checks and expert human review. The dataset captures preprocessing, functional connectivity, and graph-analysis decisions. Within these categories, steps and their sequence, software, algorithms, parameters, and supporting text spans are included where available.…

items.title: Weight locking as a safeguard for open-weight biological foundation models
items.summary: Biological foundation models can accelerate research, but their open weight release raises biosecurity concerns. A common safeguard excludes eukaryotic viral genomes from training, but fine-tuning on public viral data reverses it. We confirm that fine-tuning improves held-out viral language modelling, and that the gain comes from the viral data itself. Weight locking by spectral deformation, proposed to prevent fine-tuning, is untested in biological models. We applied it to two Evo-family models and the protein model ESM3-open, against attackers of increasing knowledge. The lock defends against the naive attacker, whose fine-tuning drives capability below pretrained on all three models. It does not defend against an informed attacker, who freezes or fuses the compensation matrix to restore near-unlocked performance.…

items.title: Machine learning cross-platform proteomic imputation enables protein quality scoring and replication of epidemiological associations
items.summary: High-throughput affinity-based proteomics has advanced biomedical research, yet fundamental, persistent discordance between mainstream platforms (SomaScan and Olink) routinely undermines the replication of findings. This platform-driven non-replication complicates downstream biological validation and biomarker prioritization. Here, we develop a machine learning-based framework for cross-platform protein value imputation to navigate this translational bottleneck. Using paired proteomic data measured by both SomaScan and Olink from 5,325 participants of the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, we developed models to impute cross-platform measurements and applied them to two independent and demographically distinct cohorts (Cardiovascular Health Study [N=3,171] and UK Biobank [UKB; N=41,405]) to evaluate downstream replication.…

items.title: Agentic Discovery Transfer Enables Cross-Cancer Discovery at Scale
items.summary: Cancer research generates tens of thousands of studies each year, yet whether a published finding holds in another cancer type or patient population is rarely tested as doing so is labor-intensive and difficult to scale. We define this task as discovery transfer and present SMART, a multi-agent large language model framework for discovery transfer in single-cell RNA-sequencing studies. Given a source manuscript and a target dataset, SMART extracts major clinical and mechanistic findings, generates and executes analyses for the testable findings, reports which findings transfer, and suggests follow-up. Applied to 121 studies across six cancer types, SMART identified findings that transfer across cancers, including a lung cancer prognostic signature that we confirmed to be associated with survival in liver cancer, pancreatic cancer and pleural mesothelioma.…

items.title: Large language models and network medicine to identify drug combinations for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer: a computational study
items.summary: Drug repurposing can accelerate therapy discovery for ER+ breast cancer, but combination selection remains difficult. We developed an LLM-driven network medicine framework that extracts drug--target relationships from 595,122 PubMed abstracts, builds a cross-model consensus network, overlays it onto the KEGG estrogen signaling pathway, and enumerates complementary drug pairs. Candidate combinations are ranked by ComboRank, which aggregates pathway coverage, LLM consensus, RAG validation, cross-method agreement, and ClinicalTrials.gov precedent. The framework identified 166 significant pairs at FDR <= 0.05, including 31 with clinical-trial precedent, with 393 shared drug--target pairs across extraction strategies and 11 exact pairs additionally supported by the pathway overlay.

items.title: Sparrowhawk: harnessing WebAssembly for private microbial genomics, and beyond
items.summary: Computational methods are a growing component of every scientific discipline, but the pace of training and expertise for using these methods has not kept up with their widening usage. Researchers expect state-of-the-art methods to be able to independently explore their results, and do so dynamically and interactively. Producing such an application which implements a new algorithm, even though it would access a much wider audience, is typically beyond the expertise and time constraints of computational method developers. Here, we show our Sparrowhawk framework can rapidly create an interactive web application to run interactive analysis on a user's machine, across a wide range of algorithms.…

items.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Raman Spectroscopy for Quantitative Prediction of Multicomponent Mixtures
items.summary: Machine Learning (ML)-assisted Raman spectroscopy that can efficiently analyze molecularly specific fingerprints is well suited for quantitative analysis of complex chemical mixtures. However, developing accurate predictive ML models for multicomponent systems remains difficult because collecting sufficient experimental calibration data is slow, expensive, and limited. In this work, we present a ML-assisted Raman spectroscopy framework for predicting the quantitative composition of multicomponent lipid mixtures (consisting of 15 lipids). To reduce the experimental burden of generating extensive multicomponent spectral datasets, we computationally constructed a large spectral library using experimentally measured pure-component Raman spectra from 15 lipids, including triglycerides, medium- and long-chain fatty acids, and fatty acid methyl and ethyl esters.…

items.title: Localizing Unsampled Regions in Partially Sampled Pathogen Phylogenies Using Machine Learning
items.summary: Motivation: Pathogen phylogenies are useful for monitoring the evolution of pathogens and for detecting new variants, as it provides information that can aid public health decisions and outbreak response. Since not all infections are sequenced, certain pathogen lineages may be missing or only poorly represented in reconstructed phylogenies. Identifying these gaps could help to determine where additional data collection is required. Results: We developed a computational method to locate regions of missing samples from the observed tree alone, without sequences from those samples. A machine learning model predicts which branches lead toward the missing region. Beam search then identifies three representative paths and estimates a candidate most recent common ancestor (MRCA) of the missing region for each path.…

items.title: Prediction and Dissection of Nitrogenase Activity Based on Protein Sequences using Dual Descriptor
items.summary: Nitrogenase reduces N2 to ammonia at ambient temperature and pressure, but its activity differs markedly among natural sequences, and conventional wet-laboratory screening suffers from low throughput and long turnaround times. Existing computational methods have partially alleviated this bottleneck, yet most of them rely on protein embeddings obtained from protein language models together with features such as gene expression, and their interpretability analyses mostly stop at the level of feature contribution. Here we present CarmnaDD, a purely sequence-driven framework built on the dual descriptor (DD): two learnable components, the composition weight map (CWM) and the position weight function (PWF), jointly generate a position-resolved description N(k), so that activity can be predicted without any prior knowledge beyond the sequence.…

items.title: PDAC BioPortal: An Integrated Web Resource for Multi-Scale Analysis of Pancreatic Cancer Transcriptomics
items.summary: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits extensive molecular heterogeneity and undergoes substantial transcriptional remodeling across disease and treatment contexts. However, publicly available PDAC transcriptomic resources remain fragmented across experimental modalities, limiting the integrated investigation of molecular programs across biological scales and cellular compartments. Here, we developed PDAC BioPortal, an integrated web-based analytical resource for multimodal interrogation of PDAC transcriptomics. The platform incorporates bulk RNA sequencing, treatment-associated transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics.…

items.title: Temporal blood sampling improves parameter recovery in a model of enterohepatic bile acid circulation using surrogate-accelerated Bayesian inference
items.summary: Bile acids (BAs) are essential signaling molecules whose enterohepatic circulation (EHC) is disrupted across hepatobiliary disorders. Despite their potential as biomarkers, clinical utility is limited by high inter-individual variability, the inability of accessible peripheral blood to reflect true hepatic exposure, and the difficulty of directly measuring key physiological parameters governing the EHC. While mechanistic models can infer inaccessible hepatic profiles and patient-specific parameters from peripheral blood, personalizing them is computationally prohibitive due to multiscale dynamics causing numerical stiffness and the thousands of evaluations required for Bayesian inference. To overcome this, we developed an accelerated Bayesian inference pipeline combining timescale model reduction with neural network surrogates.…

items.title: CHARMS and PROBAST+AI: an updated template for Data Extraction and Risk of Bias Assessment in systematic reviews of prediction models
items.summary: Background: Systematic reviews of clinical prediction models increasingly include studies using artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods alongside traditional multivariable regression approaches. A previously published Excel tool enabled standardised data extraction using the CHARMS checklist and risk of bias assessment using PROBAST. The recent publication of the PROBAST+AI framework, which distinguishes the assessment of model development quality from the assessment of model evaluation risk of bias and assesses applicability in both parts, necessitates an updated digital instrument applicable across prediction modelling methods. Methods: We updated an open-access Excel tool to incorporate the full PROBAST+AI framework.…

items.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective.…
items.tldr: A fixed set of steering vectors added to a frozen diffusion transformer recovers most of the quality gains from reinforcement learning post-training, indicating that much of the improvement comes from a constant shift rather than prompt-specific transformations.

items.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
items.summary: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos.…
items.tldr: O2LaF repurposes a shared pretrained video model to learn inverse and forward latent action dynamics from unlabeled videos, achieving state-of-the-art few-shot action probing and zero-shot action transfer.

items.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
items.summary: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid ($>250\times$ dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width extension ($d \to…

items.title: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
items.summary: Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. However, prevailing approaches often separate their visual representations or backbone computation to accommodate the different requirements of these two tasks, which limits the degree of unification. In this paper, we present HiUni, which revisits this design choice and explores whether a pretrained vision language model can be directly extended into a unified model with extensive parameter sharing. Specifically, HiUni reuses the same language-aligned ViT and dense Transformer backbone for both capabilities, while confining task-specific computation to the output side. Yet such a design introduces two key challenges. Generation in pixel space is difficult to optimize, and semantic abstraction in pretrained ViT discards fine spatial details required for synthesis.…

items.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified. To support such decisions, the Alternative Annotator Test (Alt-Test) was introduced for dense settings where all items are annotated by the same annotators. However, in many large-scale annotation settings, items are annotated by different subsets of annotators. We therefore propose the Alternative Annotator Test with Resampled Annotations (AltRA-Test), a statistical test that does not require that all items are annotated by the same annotators. AltRA-Test uses a bootstrap that resamples items, draws k human annotations for each item, and substitutes one of them with an LLM annotation. This produces paired all-human and mixed human-LLM panels.…
tags: Alternative Annotator Test with Resampled Annotations (AltRA-Test)
items.tldr: A statistical test, AltRA-Test, determines when large language models can replace human annotators by comparing inter-annotator agreement in resampled mixed human-LLM panels, and evaluations show it often requires about 100 items and makes better replacement decisions than baselines.

items.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computation. (i) Accessibility and selective access.…

items.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
items.summary: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps.…
items.tldr: AURA enables low-latency, causal video generation for streaming applications by utilizing a rolling KV cache and a two-stage distillation pipeline to significantly reduce the required diffusion steps.

items.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations.…
items.tldr: A diagnostic benchmark of 180 simulated manipulation configurations evaluates whether embodied systems can combine history-based reasoning, precise execution, and closed-loop environmental feedback, revealing that single-view competence does not transfer to composed tasks.

items.title: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
items.summary: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce \textbf{WeMM-Video}, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning. The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training and a multi-stage post-training pipeline incorporating multi-teacher OPD, anti-repetition MrDPO, and specialist RL.…
items.tldr: WeMM-Video is a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models that unify text, image, audio, and video processing for joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, using hybrid thinking modes and large-scale training to achieve strong open-source video understanding results.

items.title: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
items.summary: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. We present EgoCaptioner, which pairs a video-level overview of the setting, participants, and the wearer's overall activity with timed steps whose narration adapts to varying perceptual demands and marks key moments at specific timestamps. We develop a coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline that establishes event structure before expanding step descriptions, yielding 50,000 training examples from eight egocentric video sources.…

items.title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
items.summary: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject.…
items.tldr: SpecWM is a training-free inference framework for streaming video world models that verifies draft chunks using the target model's latent velocity field and applies reusable corrections via threshold-based accept/refine/reject decisions to improve visual quality, control, and speed.

items.title: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models
items.summary: World models aim to predict environment dynamics under actions, enabling the prediction of action consequences without executing them in the real world. Yet despite producing increasingly realistic videos, current world models often fail to capture how small action changes affect future observations. This limits their use in tasks such as robotic policy evaluation and model-based planning, where nearly identical actions can lead to qualitatively different outcomes. To address this, we propose AFFECT, an auxiliary training objective for learning the distribution of visual changes induced by action perturbations. Specifically, we inject temporally correlated noise into the actions of a policy trained on task-agnostic human teleoperation.…
items.tldr: AFFECT, an auxiliary objective that trains world models to match visual responses to temporally correlated action noise, improves rollout fidelity and planning success in simulated and real robotic tasks.

items.title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
items.summary: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same? CAPTCHAs offer a natural test, since humans solve them through this very loop, clicking and dragging on the screen and adjusting after each result. Yet existing CAPTCHA benchmarks are largely solved and rarely spatial, while spatial benchmarks rarely require action. We therefore present TuringSpace, a synthetic web environment of 125 interactive CAPTCHAs that span five spatial abilities and must be solved through clicks and drags on the screen. Every task is a program that generates new instances with a checker and an oracle, so the tasks also form a scalable training gym.…

items.title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
items.summary: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. We propose Skill-FT (Skill-Guided Fine-Tuning), which uses natural-language skills to suppress undesirable habits and elicit underrepresented effective behaviors during teacher rollouts, then fine-tunes a target model on the resulting trajectories. We introduce AutoMaster, an autonomous post-training system in which an LLM agent develops these interventions through trajectory analysis, skill design, data selection, and feedback from rollouts and target-model evaluation.…

items.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
items.summary: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime. We release code and weights at https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-depth-pro-2/
items.tldr: A single scalable network estimates dense metric depth for images and video at native resolution, jointly improving metric accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency.

items.title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
items.summary: Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics. However, how to construct proxies and prompts for optimal downstream quality remains underexplored, as do the capabilities and limitations of this paradigm. Through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation, we study proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting. The results reveal task-dependent trade-offs: coarse proxies favor natural motion, while medium-grained proxies favor consistency. Physics simulation and proxy-aligned prompting further improve average quality. Guided by these findings, we introduce Coda-DaVinci, a task-adaptive agentic framework for Code2Video generation that selects between proxy-guided and direct generation, adapts modeling granularity to each entity, and coordinates simulation with proxy-grounded prompting.…
items.tldr: A task-adaptive agentic framework utilizes 3D proxies, physics simulation, and multi-agent coordination to enhance the structural control, physical plausibility, and visual realism of generated videos.

items.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
items.summary: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training.…
items.tldr: Posterior Matching Distillation trains a stochastic student to match a teacher diffusion model’s full posterior via tilted mean constraints, enabling high-quality few-step image generation without auxiliary score networks.

items.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
items.summary: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves effective navigation with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain. Rather than teaching the brain to predict geometric goals, we equip it with a semantic tool-calling interface for conveying movement decisions to an action expert in natural language. We first adapt the action expert to carry out these movement requests, then jointly improve the brain's movement decisions and the action expert's continuous execution through closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL).…
items.tldr: ZeroVLN is a slow-fast vision-language navigation framework that avoids navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning of the VLM brain by using a semantic tool-calling interface and closed-loop reinforcement learning to coordinate a language-based brain with an action expert, improving VLN-CE…

items.title: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. However, it is unknown how dedicated training of these networks can contribute to the successes of weight-space programming. We present a benchmark of LLM-driven weight-space programming on vision models, in which five LLMs edit convolutional networks and vision transformers on relabeling and error-correction tasks on Waterbirds, CIFAR-100, PACS and Entity-30. We report more than 2,600 such edit processes, whereby each edit is scored on held-out images for success, side effects and accuracy loss. We compare standard training with label smoothing, gradient-based editable training, and our Edit-Ready Training (ERT), a novel method that rehearses the direct, closed-form weight edits LLMs perform.…

items.title: Accelerating Mixture of Block Attention via Dynamic Routing, KV-Centric Execution and Runtime Pipelining
items.summary: Mixture of Block Attention (MoBA) reduces long-context computation by selecting key-value (KV) blocks for each query. FlashMoBA implements MoBA efficiently but retains a fixed Top-k budget and query-centric schedule. Fixed Top-k applies one budget across different score distributions and couples routing to task granularity; query-range ownership fragments K/V reuse when several ranges select the same column. We present LightningMoBA, which co-designs selection and execution through dynamic routing, KV-centric ownership, and runtime pipelining. Dynamic routing thresholds MoBA's per-query block scores and directly emits variable-cardinality sparse metadata. KV-centric ownership groups selected rows by (query head, KV block) column, splits high-fanout columns into bounded tasks, and reuses each task's loaded KV tile.…
items.tldr: LightningMoBA combines dynamic routing, KV-centric ownership, and runtime pipelining to accelerate long-context attention while maintaining or improving quality.

items.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
items.summary: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution. Existing online detectors do not use the instruction text, while instruction-conditioned methods operate offline. In this paper, we study online, instruction-conditioned mistake detection in egocentric videos. Using only observed video, task instructions, and prior predictions, our model identifies and localizes completed action attempts and classifies them as correct, modified, slip, corrections, or additions; omitted steps are determined after the video ends.…

items.title: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
items.summary: Peer review relies on several readers finding different problems. We measure critique overlap in conference and journal reviews. At ICLR, measured overlap rose from 12.0% in 2026 to 21.3% in 2027, in reviews from the same stage of the review process, with year-on-year rises at NeurIPS, ICML and the F1000 and PLOS journals. A third ICLR review of a paper added 5.46 new problems to the other two in 2027, against 6.12 in 2026. We apply MELD, a detector of LLM-generated text, to all reviews. Within a paper, two reviews that MELD flags overlap more than two unflagged reviews: by 3.0 points at ICLR in 2024-2025, by 4.5 points in 2026-2027, and by 5.4 points across five journal sources.…
items.tldr: Critique overlap among peer reviews is rising, and reviews identified as LLM-generated are less distinct from each other, indicating decreasing diversity of critiques.

items.title: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain
items.summary: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. Despite their architectural differences, these methods all share the same premise: geometry is first compressed into a latent space and only then modeled by the generator. We take a different route and propose Direct3D-V3, a latent-free diffusion transformer (DiT) framework that discards the VAE altogether and operates in the native voxel domain, directly modeling raw SDF voxel grids during both training and sampling.…

items.title: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
items.summary: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates. Evaluating the third ability requires reliably executing an experiment that an agent designs, with readings grounded in a real laboratory. We introduce TwinLab-Bench, which evaluates AI scientists on self-designed experiments in 52 tasks from laboratories in the physical sciences, the life sciences, and engineering. The benchmark supports more than 100 experimental action types, and the agent's report is scored by comparison with a hidden answer taken from real laboratory records.…

items.title: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions
items.summary: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly integrated into everyday life, their ability to provide safe and reliable assistance in realistic daily activities remains insufficiently explored. Existing safety benchmarks primarily focus on isolated harmful requests or adversarial scenarios, overlooking the safety risks that may arise as ordinary tasks unfold. In practice, users pursue legitimate goals through multi-turn, multimodal interactions, where seemingly benign requests may become safety-critical when considered alongside earlier actions and visual observations. This calls for Dynamic Safety Awareness, the ability to track evolving task conditions, recognize implicit contextual risks, and provide safe and helpful assistance.…
items.tldr: A new benchmark, DailySafe, evaluates the ability of multimodal large language models to maintain safety and address evolving risks within complex, multi-turn, real-world interactions.

items.title: Suppressing the Shortcut Hidden Behind the Gains of VideoLLM Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is the stage in which Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) advance their capability to reason over video. However, the VideoLLM also learns to answer from textual regularities of its training data, a shortcut that bypasses the video. The regularities behind the shortcut are hard to define at the data level, and the shortcut forms regardless of training epoch, data size, or backbone. The shortcut is hidden behind a rise in accuracy within the training distribution, yet it is not required for the rise and even costs SFT the gain the video offers under distribution shift. We therefore propose Video-Evidence Training via Orthogonal projection (VETO), which intervenes on the fine-tuning update where the shortcut is written rather than on the data.…
items.tldr: VETO suppresses shortcut learning in VideoLLMs by projecting supervised fine-tuning updates onto the orthogonal complement of the text-only activation subspace, improving out-of-distribution video reasoning.

items.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
items.summary: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game.…
items.tldr: PlayCraft uses a vision-based player agent and a crafter agent to iteratively revise games, improving player learning gains and slopes across intelligence settings.

items.title: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis
items.summary: Facial deepfake detectors are usually trained on blending fakes, where a generated face is pasted back into a real frame. Recent generators synthesize the entire face and leave no traces of blending. On a benchmark of 19 datasets released from 2019 to 2026, the best prior facial deepfake detector reaches a mean AUROC of 96.2% on ten blending datasets, but none exceeds 78.1% on five datasets of entire face synthesis (EFS). AI-generated content (AIGC) detectors do not close this gap. We propose TwinD, a detector trained on FaceForensics++ fakes and two kinds of twins: fakes made from a real frame. A reconstruction twin is a real frame reconstructed by an autoencoder, with the real pixels put back in a random region. It targets the neural traces of a decoder. A blob twin blends an altered copy of a real frame with the frame itself, targeting blending artifacts.…
items.tldr: TwinD, trained on reconstruction and blob twins derived from real frames, detects both blending and entire-face-synthesis deepfakes, improving AUROC over prior detectors.

items.title: WITHDRAWN: Identifying Phelan-McDermid-Like Electrophysiological Subtypes in Autism Using EEG and Machine Learning
items.summary: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript until a re-evaluation of the clinical data is completed. Therefore, the authors do not wish this work to be cited as reference for the project. If you have any questions, please contact the corresponding author.

items.title: Quantifying Support for Competing Biomedical Hypotheses using Large Language Models and Bayesian Analysis
items.summary: Background: Comparing competing biomedical hypotheses can help researchers prioritize questions for further investigation. Literature-based evaluation systems such as SKiM-GPT assess support for individual hypotheses, but independently assigned scores may not clearly distinguish their relative support. Direct comparison, accompanied by uncertainty estimates, could help researchers interpret the balance of evidence and track how it changes over time. Results: We introduce KM-GPT-DCH, an extension of SKiM-GPT that integrates co-occurrence-based literature retrieval with large language models to directly compare support for two user-defined biomedical hypotheses. The system evaluates sampled sets of relevant PubMed abstracts using a structured scoring approach and applies a Bayesian model to estimate relative literature support and its uncertainty.…

items.title: Lightweight and Explainable AI for Chest Radiograph Classification in Low-Resource Settings: Cross-Dataset Generalization, Grad-CAM Verification, and Uncertainty-Aware Referral
items.summary: Chest radiography is the most common imaging test worldwide, yet models trained on one hospital's data often fail elsewhere, a critical problem for low-resource hospitals that cannot collect large local datasets. This paper presents a lightweight, explainable framework for chest radiograph classification, trained and evaluated entirely on CPU with public data. EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet-18 are trained on a 10,000-image subset of NIH ChestX-ray14 and evaluated without retraining on a paediatric pneumonia set, alongside a TorchXRayVision DenseNet121 pretrained baseline and a model trained directly on paediatric data. On the NIH test set (n = 2,500), the best single model reaches pneumonia AUC-ROC 0.738 and a two-model ensemble 0.742, while an adult-trained model falls to AUC 0.454 on paediatric images, and, symmetrically, a paediatric-trained model falls to 0.473 on adult NIH images.…

items.title: The Shrinking Grace Period and the Downsizing of Ransomware Victims: Exploitation Timelines and Breach Size Among US Health Care Providers, 2016-2026
items.summary: Objectives: To examine how quickly software vulnerabilities are exploited after public disclosure, and whether hacking breaches at US health care providers changed in size after 2021, a period in which earlier studies had found attacks concentrating on large organizations. Methods: Retrospective analysis of public data. We linked the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (1,748 entries) with CVE publication dates to measure time to confirmed exploitation by half-year of publication (2021-2025). We also analyzed 8,029 breach reports submitted to the HHS Office for Civil Rights, focusing on hacking/IT incidents at health care providers.…

items.title: Cross-Scanner Reliability of Brain MRI Foundation Models: A Travelling-Heads Study
items.summary: Foundation models (FMs) are increasingly used for brain MRI analysis, but their reliability across scanners remains unclear. We evaluated seven FMs using 120 acquisitions from 20 participants in the ON-Harmony travelling-heads dataset. We also used a separate cohort of 1,411 healthy adults to train brain-age predictors, either by fitting Ridge regression to frozen embeddings or by fine-tuning the models. We assessed how accurately they predicted age and how consistently their embeddings and age predictions behaved across scanners. AnatCL and y-Aware produced the most reliable embeddings, with distance-based intraclass correlation coefficients (dbICC) of 0.91-0.92, approaching 0.95 for FreeSurfer-derived anatomical measurements. Their shared anatomical preprocessing emerged as a plausible contributor to this pattern.…

items.title: An LLM-assisted Pipeline for Identifying ClinicalTrials.gov Registry Changes and Their Association with Primary Endpoint Positivity
items.summary: Registration of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) in a public registry such as ClinicalTrials.gov should minimize the risk of reporting bias. However, records may be modified during a trial and the resulting discrepancies are not always apparent without a detailed examination of all version histories, a process that is cumbersome when performed manually. We developed an automated workflow to investigate whether specific changes to RCT registry entries are associated with primary endpoint positivity. Our pipeline extracts RCT records from ClinicalTrials.gov and systematically detects changes between successive versions using a combination of deterministic textual analysis and large language model (LLM)-assisted classification.…

items.title: Prospective prediction of clinical trial outcomes from public evidence
items.summary: Predicting clinical trial outcomes requires interpreting biological and clinical evidence in the context of a specific intervention, population and study design. Here we test whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can predict trial outcomes from publicly available evidence. We introduce TrialDossier, which assembles standardized evidence dossiers, and TrialOutlook, which uses these dossiers with GPT-5 to estimate the probability that a trial meets its prespecified primary endpoint. Among 694 ongoing trials with results expected within six months of cohort assembly, 69 outcomes first disclosed after forecast recording had been adjudicated by 20 October 2026. TrialOutlook achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.819 (95% confidence interval, 0.708 to 0.914) and an average precision of 0.860.…

items.title: ADSMoE: A mixture-of-experts-based transformer autoencoder for discovering multimodal Alzheimer's disease subtypes
items.summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits substantial biological and clinical heterogeneity, posing critical challenges for advancing precision medicine. Existing data-driven approaches often rely on modality-specific clustering or predefined biomarker trajectories, limiting their ability to discover disease subtypes from incomplete, heterogeneous real-world data. In this study, we introduce ADSMoE, a mixture-of-experts (MoE)-based multimodal representation learning framework that jointly identifies AD subtypes as latent disease signatures while accommodating incomplete modality combinations. ADSMoE integrates a Fleximodal MoE encoder that accommodates arbitrary combinations of available modalities with a novel subtype-specific MoE decoder to capture complementary disease characteristics through expert specialization.…

items.title: Generative Deep Learning Maps Brain Oxygen Metabolism and Its Age-Related Decline from Two Standard Noninvasive MRI Scans
items.summary: Purpose: To develop a generative deep learning model mapping the cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) from minimal, contrast-free MRI. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study used 3-T MRI of healthy adults from one center (May 2015-June 2025). A conditional generative adversarial network (GAN) was trained to reproduce contrast-based analytical CMRO2 from progressively fewer quantitative MRI inputs (cerebral blood flow [CBF], T2*, T2, cerebral blood volume), T1-weighted MRI, or resting-state functional MRI. Models were trained on 54 participants and tested on 41 (25 women; mean age, 49 years +/- 23 [SD]), on calculation-task data, and, without retraining, on same-protocol (n = 24) and cross-vendor (n = 12) data.…

items.title: Virtual spatial transcriptomics links kidney histopathology to disease-associated molecular programs
items.summary: Introduction: Spatial transcriptomics can resolve compartment-specific molecular programs in kidney disease, but its cost and technical requirements limit its use in clinical diagnostics and in large biopsy archives. Predicting spatial gene expression from routine histology with artificial intelligence could extend molecular characterization to existing clinically annotated kidney tissue collections. Methods: We adapted DeepSpot-M, a pretrained multimodal foundation model that predicts spatial gene expression from histology, using paired hematoxylin and eosin images and Visium spatial transcriptomics from 209 Kidney Precision Medicine Project (KPMP) participants.…

items.title: Multimodal population-scale cell atlases define archetypes and extremes of human blood
items.summary: The cellular composition of blood is fundamental to human physiology and is routinely measured to assess health and disease. Circulating immune cells show extensive heterogeneity, but the organising principles and extremes of variation across individuals remain undefined. Here, using single-cell transcriptomics across two biobank cohorts encompassing ~6,000 individuals, we show that human blood occupies recurrent archetypal states defined by coordinated cell composition patterns. We delineate three major archetypes spanning naive lymphoid, myeloid and cytotoxic composition, and two minor archetypes characterised by type I interferon-driven inflammation and expanded premalignant CD5+ B cells.…

items.title: MRCAT: A multi-agent framework for reliable Mendelian randomization analysis and causal interpretation
items.summary: Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants to estimate causal effects of exposures on health outcomes, but rigorous MR analyses require coordinated procedures and interpretation under explicit methodological assumptions. Although artificial intelligence (AI) agents can automate analyses, computational completion does not guarantee scientific reliability. Here, we present MRCAT, a multi-agent framework that translates MR-specific knowledge into an AI-assisted workflow that is plannable, executable, verifiable, recoverable and traceable. MRCAT combines dependency-aware planning, Skill-guided execution and expert-informed review with traceable reporting guided by STROBE-MR, a guideline for clear and transparent reporting of MR studies, and iterative Writer-Judge checking.…

items.title: Using a large language model as the primary coder in health content analysis: a verification framework, per-variable reliability and proposed reporting items.
items.summary: Objective: To describe and evaluate a framework for using a large language model (LLM) as the primary coder in health content analysis, and to propose reporting items for LLM assisted studies, because no reporting standard exists. Methods: An LLM coded 6,982 Instagram and TikTok posts using a human written, human calibrated instrument. The framework has six components: human authorship of the instrument; two round human calibration; source discipline; quote anchored coding; verification in a representative and an outcome enriched sample, blinded in both directions; and per variable reliability reporting against a prespecified threshold, with the consequence of failure fixed in advance. Agreement was measured with Gwets AC1, prespecified because the outcome distribution was heavily skewed.…

items.title: Real-World Cuff-Measured Blood Pressure Trajectories in 20,003 Consumer Wearable Users
items.summary: Consumer wearables increasingly allow users to log cuff-measured blood pressure (BP), but resulting BP trajectories are uncharacterized. In this retrospective cohort study, 20,003 adults with Elevated BP or Stage 1 or Stage 2 Hypertension logged BP via a consumer wearable platform. We modeled 6-month trajectories with linear mixed-effects models and examined associations of [≥]5 mmHg reduction with engagement and wearable-derived metrics. Adjusted systolic reductions ranged from -2.6 mmHg (95% CI -3.1 to -2.2) in Elevated BP to -12.1 mmHg (-12.5 to -11.7) in Stage 2 Hypertension; diastolic reductions were -3.7 and -9.2 mmHg in Stage 1 and Stage 2. Overall, 50.2% achieved a [≥]5 mmHg systolic reduction and 27.9% reached normal BP.…

items.title: AortoBVI: A Machine Learning-derived Risk Stratification of Ascending Aortic Aneurysms Predictable by Imaging
items.summary: Background: Current diameter-based risk stratification for ascending aortic aneurysms incompletely captures patient-specific dissection risk. Here, we apply machine learning to ex vivo aortic biomechanics to define a tissue-derived risk continuum, termed aortic biomechanical vulnerability index (AortoBVI), and use magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to predict this index in vivo. Methods: Ascending aortic tissue from 353 aneurysms, 45 normal aortas, and 46 acute aortic dissections underwent biomechanical testing.
