items.tldr: Agent evolution is often bottlenecked by noisy evaluations that cannot reliably identify better candidate artifacts or rank methods, so progress requires making true improvements detectable and accumulable.

items.title: FVScore: Specification-Driven Neuro-Symbolic Video Evaluation
items.summary: We introduce Faithfulness Video Score (FVSCORE), a neuro-symbolic framework for specification-driven video generation evaluation. Existing evaluators rely on holistic MLLM judgments or vision-language metrics, yet aligning their scores with human judgments and tracing them to specific temporal violations remain open challenges. FVSCORE addresses these limitations by compiling each video into explicit propositions capturing prompt requirements and implicit propositions capturing unstated physical, temporal, and cross-modal constraints. It grounds each proposition using specialized perceptual tools and evaluates the resulting confidence traces with soft temporal operators inspired by Linear Temporal Logic.…
items.tldr: FVSCORE is a neuro-symbolic evaluation framework that compiles videos into prompt and implicit constraint propositions, verifies them with perceptual tools and soft temporal logic, and calibrates significant violations to produce interpretable, human-aligned feedback for video generation.

items.title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus
items.summary: Deep models often rely on spurious correlations that fail on underrepresented groups. Existing methods either correct human-specified bias attributes or infer unknown biases from the learned representation space. However, annotated attributes may differ from the shortcuts actually used by a model, while a single representation provides incomplete and potentially noisy evidence. Our key insight is that a bias obscured in one feature space may be clearer in another. In this work, we propose CHORD (Cross-view Harmonic Outlier Reversal for Debiasing), a multi-view framework that allows samples to "sing in chorus" across diverse representation spaces to achieve robust cross-view consensus. CHORD aggregates aggregates within-class partitions in each view, which is a proxy for specifying candidate biases, to debias the target representation and classifier without bias supervision.…
items.tldr: A multi-view debiasing method aggregates within-class partitions across diverse representation spaces to reduce reliance on spurious correlations and improve worst-group accuracy without bias supervision.

items.title: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. We reimagine PSS for LLMs as a sequential process over the whole stream and propose RICoT (Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought), a prompting framework that works through the pages as a reader would: within a sliding window it reasons about each page and commits its boundary decision before moving on, and across windows it carries forward a compact record of what it has read, keeping per-call cost bounded. We also introduce FinancePSS-205, a benchmark of 205 real-world, de-identified financial page streams, to be released publicly.…

items.title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: Latent diffusion models rely on a decoder to map denoised latents to pixels, adding complexity and inference cost. We introduce Decoding Without a Decoder (DWD), which lets a finetuned diffusion transformer produce final pixels directly through a linear head. Unlike previous methods, where the denoising output leads to final pixels, DWD separates the two roles: the original denoising head continues to drive sampling, then the new DWD head predicts the pixels at the final step. We extend pretrained latent models with DWD efficiently by finetuning only the last few transformer blocks, training the DWD head with pixel quality losses while anchoring the denoising head to the pretrained model to preserve the sample trajectory. Across latent image and video generators, DWD removes the decoder and reduces inference cost while maintaining or even improving pixel quality.…
items.tldr: A method that removes the decoder from latent diffusion models by adding a final-step prediction head to a finetuned diffusion transformer, reducing inference cost and improving pixel quality in image and video generation.

items.title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisions.…
items.tldr: Across three shopping benchmarks, increasing large language model shopping agents' thinking effort did not statistically improve product-choice quality but significantly raised reported confidence, and most models were poorly calibrated with correlated errors.

items.title: Attenuated, Not Absent. Trusting Autonomous Systems Tracks Reliability More Closely, With Less Neural Engagement, Than Trusting Humans
items.summary: Users of autonomous systems and AI assistants decide whether to accept a system's output, yet whether such active trust decisions engage the same evaluative architecture as trust between people remains unknown. Forty-four participants made trial-by-trial decisions to trust or distrust a human or autonomous system partner during fMRI, with identical prescripted accuracy for both partners across five difficulty levels. Despite equivalent performance, trust in humans exceeded their reliability. At the highest difficulty level, the estimated probability of trusting the human partner was 72% but only 51% for the system, despite both performing at 52% accuracy. Distrust decisions recruited a prespecified performance monitoring network of valuation, salience, social-perceptual and affective regions. On hard trials, this network remained functionally coupled for both partners.…

items.title: In silico designed small molecule targets misfolded TDP-43 to rescue function and ALS pathology
items.summary: The DNA/RNA binding protein TARDBP or TDP-43 is a key driver of pathology in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), a motor neuron disease with no known cure. In >97% of sporadic ALS patients, nuclear TDP-43 in motor neurons mislocalizes and aggregates in the cellular cytoplasm (gain-of-function). A parallel reduction in nuclear TDP-43 in ALS patients leads to a loss-of-function in mRNA binding and splicing regulation. Using our machine learning platform, we discovered ACE-339, a novel, orally bioavailable small molecule that disrupts insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Using in vitro, in vivo and in silico models, we show that ACE-339 directly targets aggregated forms of TDP-43. ACE-339 interacts directly with TDP-43 hexamers, disaggregates recombinant TDP-43 and rescues both gain- and loss-of-function phenotypes of TDP-43 in cells.…

items.title: Elucidating the Sodium Channel-Targeting Anti-Seizure Medication Interactome: A Drug-Target Pathway Analysis
items.summary: Epilepsy is a common neurological disorder in both children and adults, primarily managed with anti-seizure medications (ASMs). Sodium channel blockers are among the most commonly used ASMs. These medications exhibit distinct spectra of efficacy and side effect profiles. These likely result from different off-target interactions, protein binding profiles, and subunit selectivity that remain poorly characterized. We developed a neural network-based computational pipeline to systematically elucidate the molecular targets and associated biological pathways of selected sodium channel-modulating ASMs: carbamazepine, lamotrigine, eslicarbazepine, licarbazepine, lacosamide, phenytoin, and cenobamate. Using the DRIFT (Drug-target identification based on chemical similarity) algorithm for proteome-wide target prediction, we identified protein targets for these ASMs.…

items.title: Scaling up naturalistic narrative research: A reproducible large language model-based tool for evaluating contextual information gain
items.summary: Narratives are a universal part of natural human experience. As experimental stimuli, narratives allow scientists to study complex mental processes with direct relevance to everyday experience. These analyses typically require manual labeling of key event features. Such characterization of narrative stimuli are extremely labor-intensive and prone to subjectivity. Automated tools could reduce these difficulties and enable scaling to longer, varied stimuli by exposing the exact quantities computed. We address this by introducing a metric that uses open-weight LLMs to compute contextual information gain. Our metric correlates with human ratings of event importance and causal centrality, critically distinguishing the latter from semantic centrality, thus overcoming limitations of existing automated tools.…

items.title: Characterization of heterogeneous bioinformatics training needs in the AI era
items.summary: Bioinformatics training providers serve heterogeneous audiences, and generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly changing what learners need. Training-needs surveys are typically analyzed question by question or split by demographics such as career stage. This assumes that people in the same demographic group need the same training, whereas needs may depend more on the data people work with. We present a protocol that groups survey respondents by the similarity of their topic ratings rather than by demographics. Respondents form a correlation network, and community detection identifies learner profiles with shared needs.…

items.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Antibiotic Resistance Genes: Performance, Interpretability, and Cross-Database Redundancy
items.summary: Antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) classifiers are typically developed and evaluated within a single curated database, leaving open how much two independently curated databases agree and what that implies for apparent cross-database generalization. We trained an XGBoost classifier on amino acid trigram frequencies and physicochemical descriptors using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD), the field's largest curated ARG resource. The model separated resistance genes from non-resistance proteins with near-ceiling accuracy (AUROC = 0.982, MCC = 0.886); a label-shuffling null baseline collapsed to chance (AUROC = 0.508) and bootstrap confidence intervals were narrow, confirming genuine signal rather than data leakage or overfitting.…

items.title: Decompose and Recompose: Reference-Centered Multimodal Adaptation of Protein Language Models for Enzyme Turnover Prediction
items.summary: Predicting enzyme turnover numbers ($k_{\mathrm{cat}}$) from protein sequences and reaction chemistry helps prioritize candidates in virtual screening. Reliable ranking requires distinguishing activity differences between enzyme--reaction pairs. Recent interaction models combine enzyme and chemical information, but two representation challenges remain. First, reactants and products have distinct roles in catalysis: reactants are recognized and transformed, whereas products are formed and released. Yet these models merge the two sides before enzyme interaction, leaving the enzyme's response to each role implicit. Second, enzyme representations produced by cross-attention mix reaction-dependent changes with an enzyme-specific background shared across chemical conditions. This mixture can obscure activity-relevant differences between samples.…

items.title: A Biologically Interpretable Single-Cell Pathology Foundation Model for Molecular Decoding of H&E Images
items.summary: The microscopic structure of human tissues encodes molecular information that is not directly accessible by visual inspection. Current pathology foundation models improve histological interpretation but operate at multicellular resolution. It remains unclear whether routine histology contains structured molecular and cellular information recoverable at single-cell resolution, which biological properties are associated with this recoverability, and where its limits lie. Here, we introduce Loki2, a single-cell pathology foundation model trained on UniSeg, a pan-tissue resource integrating 15 million cells with segmentation, lineage annotations and measured or histology-inferred transcriptomic profiles. We examine the above question across cellular representation, molecular recoverability, and patient-level relevance.…

items.title: Savant: A Fast, Structure-Free Binding Affinity Predictor For Protein-Ligand Drug Screening
items.summary: Protein-ligand binding affinity determines which of many candidate molecules is worth synthesizing and assaying, making it the central measurement in early drug discovery. Binding affinity is commonly expressed as the dissociation constant, an equilibrium measure that indicates how easily a complex separates into its components. AI-based generative chemistry and make-on-demand chemical catalogs now produce molecules faster than rigorous method can evaluate them. Leading computational methods co-fold the complex before scoring the binding affinity between the protein and the ligand, which provides high accuracy but requires a graphics processing unit (GPU) and substantial time for every pair evaluated.Here we present Savant, a machine learning model that estimates the dissociation constant using only the protein's amino acid sequence and the ligand's structure written as a line of text…

items.title: Casanovo-TMT: deep learning-based de novo sequencing of TMTpro-labeled peptides and phosphopeptides
items.summary: De novo peptide sequencing reads peptides directly from tandem mass spectra, but none of the released deep learning models can sequence peptides labeled with isobaric tags such as TMTpro, which are widely used for multiplexed quantitative proteomics. We extended the residue vocabulary of Casanovo with TMTpro tags and phosphorylation, fine-tuned it on 21 million spectra from our laboratory, most of them TMTpro-labeled, and re-ranked the candidates in the beam by their agreement with the measured precursor mass. The resulting model, Casanovo-TMT, predicted the exact peptidoform for 84.7% of the TMTpro-labeled spectra in our test set and for 87.4 and 79.6% of the spectra in two public global-proteome datasets from other laboratories, whereas the extended vocabulary without fine-tuning gave 0.3%.…

items.title: Sequence-based models predict TF binding with negligible contributions from motif cooperativity
items.summary: How transcription factors (TFs) selectively recognize their genomic targets among numerous sites containing similar DNA motifs remains an open question. Cooperative binding at neighboring motif sites is widely considered a key mechanism of TF specificity, yet its genome-wide contribution remains unclear. Machine learning models can now predict TF binding directly from DNA sequence, providing opportunities to investigate its underlying determinants. Here, we leveraged BPNet models trained on ~2,000 ENCODE TF binding profiles to systematically assess motif cooperativity. Although detected at individual loci, cooperativity made a negligible contribution to genome-wide binding predictions. Nevertheless, the models captured differences in binding preferences between TFs with similar motif preferences, even within the same cellular environment.…

items.title: Pharmacophore-Inspired Virtual Receptor: Generating Realistic Peptide Binding Data for Machine Learning
items.summary: VReceptor is a virtual receptor simulation framework that generates realistic, sequence-dependent binding data for peptide-based therapeutics. It combines pharmacophore-inspired weighting schemes with amino acid similarity metrics to evaluate peptide design strategies in a controlled environment. Validation using the Prolactin-Releasing Peptide (PrRP) dataset confirms VReceptor's ability to approximate binding behaviours and optimize experimental planning. This framework empowers researchers in computational peptide design and active learning workflows while highlighting areas for further refinement.

items.title: Segment Anything for Microscopy 2
items.summary: Foundation models have advanced microscopy image segmentation, but existing models are trained on two-dimensional data, struggle with complex structures in volumetric data, and address only a narrow range of analysis tasks. Here we present Segment Anything for Microscopy 2 (SAM2), a foundation model that adapts SAM2 to joint 2D and 3D segmentation in light and electron microscopy. Trained on annotations of more than 23 million cells and nuclei and 1.6 million cellular structures, SAM2 achieves state-of-the-art automatic and interactive segmentation and outperforms generalist and specialist methods on volumetric data. Dedicated models further enable accurate mitochondrion and nucleus segmentation in electron microscopy. Beyond segmentation, SAM2 supports pixel and object classification from few annotations as well as cell tracking in 2D and 3D time-lapse data.…

items.title: FoldMapper: Protein Inverse Folding Model with Structure-Derived Evolutionary Profiles and a Multiscale Graph Encoder
items.summary: Protein inverse folding designs amino-acid sequences that fold into a target backbone structure. Existing deep-learning methods exploit backbone geometry but not evolutionary statistics. Those statistics come from a multiple sequence alignment, which must be built from a query sequence. That query is the sequence to be designed, so the dependency is circular. We present FoldMapper, an inverse folding model that breaks this circularity. It retrieves structural homologues by shape alone, then aggregates their amino-acid identities into a per-residue structural position-specific frequency (SPSF) profile. A Multiscale Graph Encoder passes a sparse profile-conditioned encoding into a dense structure-conditioned message-passing network. FoldMapper reaches 60.0% best-of-100 sequence recovery on TED domains, 64.9% on PDB, and 51.3%/53.1% on PPIBindBench non-peptide and peptide binders.…

items.title: S-PLM-TM enables fast and accurate sequence-based search for remote homologs
items.summary: Protein structures and functions can remain conserved after extensive sequence divergence, but detecting these distant relationships across large databases remains challenging. Here we present S-PLM-TM, a sequence-only remote homology search tool based on a structure-aware protein language model. Cross-modal flow matching and contrastive learning incorporate structural information into sequence representations. A lightweight calibration head enables structural-similarity search with the frozen encoder, while a residue-level alignment head generates structural alignments directly from sequence. S-PLM-TM outperforms the tested sequence-based methods in remote homology detection, rivals structure-based methods in structural classification and retrieves the most functionally consistent neighbors.…

items.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Missense Variant Pathogenicity Prediction in the KCNQ Gene Family
items.summary: Missense variants in the KCNQ family of voltage-gated potassium channel genes are associated with a broad spectrum of neurological and cardiac disorders for which computational tools capable of differentiating benign and pathogenic variants are essential. Here, we present, to our knowledge, the first application of quantum machine learning (QML) to missense pathogenicity prediction. We employ a hybrid quantum framework combining data re-uploading quantum neural networks with quantum support vector machines and applied it to pathogenicity classification across the full KCNQ gene family.…

items.title: Automated segmentation of renal structures using brightfield images of unstained kidney biopsies
items.summary: The automated segmentation of unstained kidney brightfield microscopy images remains a significant challenge in medical imaging. In conventional histopathology, staining provides crucial structural and molecular contrast, allowing renal compartments and structures to be readily distinguished. The absence of staining markedly reduces this contrast, obscuring the fine architectural details that are essential for diagnosis. Addressing this gap would reduce reliance on staining protocols, reduce technical and interpretive variability, and preserve valuable tissue for downstream molecular or multi-omics analyses. Ultimately, automation of unstained image segmentation could enable faster, more objective tissue analysis while preserving samples for further molecular testing.…

items.title: Deciphering the Biological Function of Tandem Mass Spectra Using a Dual-Modal Metabolite Language Model
items.summary: Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry untargeted metabolomics captures thousands of metabolic peaks from biological samples. Conventional identification-dependent metabolomics workflows require confident structural annotation before identified features can enter downstream pathway or functional analysis. However, only a small fraction of detected metabolic features can be assigned confident structural annotations, leaving a large fraction difficult to incorporate into downstream biological interpretation, a form of "functional dark matter". Here, we introduce Spec2Function, a function-centric framework that infers biological functions from tandem mass spectrometry (MS2) spectra. Spec2Function is trained using characterized spectrum-text pairs but does not require prior structural identification of the query spectra at inference time.…

items.title: statLens enables accurate and interpretable statistical intelligence
items.summary: Diverse existing approaches and analyses of large-scale biomedical omics datasets along with the complexity of the corresponding statistical analytical workflows pose challenges to the direct application of large language models (LLMs) to data analysis tasks. We present statLens, a model-agnostic AI-driven statistical intelligence framework that integrates LLMs, code and human review. We demonstrate statLens using differential expression analysis across heterogeneous biomedical data as a use case. On 102 benchmark tasks from 74 datasets across six omics modalities, statLens maintained consistently high accuracy (92.5--95.0\%) across seven language models and outperformed LLM-only inference (17.5--46.8\%), whereas autonomous-agent accuracy varied widely (58.7--99.5\%).…

items.title: HyperGenie: A method for predicting enzymatic gene essentiality using hypergraph neural networks and genome-scale metabolic models
items.summary: Identifying essential genes in bacteria is crucial for drug discovery and synthetic biology. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) evaluated via flux balance analysis remain standard, yet they rely on the often-invalid premise that mutant strains optimize for maximum growth. Recent machine learning approaches circumvent this limitation using random forests or graph neural networks on mass flow graphs (MFGs). However, data-driven tools like random forests discard network topology, while graph-based tools like MFGs decompose multi-component biochemical reactions into pairwise interactions, misrepresenting complex stoichiometry and limiting interpretability. Furthermore, existing methods remain largely uncharacterised in data-scarce regimes and cross-environmental conditions.…

items.title: MorphoStain: Physics-Guided Latent Diffusion and Morphological Distillation for Multiplex Stain Decomposition in Alzheimer's Neuropathology
items.summary: Multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) enables simultaneous biomarker profiling, yet unmixing co-localized targets with identical spectra, such as dual-DAB marking of Tau and Amyloid-beta in Alzheimer's pathology, remains mathematically ill-posed. We propose MorphoStain, an unsupervised, physics-guided framework for morphological stain decomposition with epistemic uncertainty quantification. MorphoStain models stain separation via a conditional Latent Diffusion Teacher operating on a Beer-Lambert optical-density manifold, guided by pathology foundation models. To enable real-time clinical throughput, the teacher is distilled into a FastStudentU-Net (0.12M parameters, > 1,400x compression), while a Symmetric Morphological Routing Module dynamically disentangles identical chromogen overlap.…

items.title: Changes in Resting-State Functional Network Specialization in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
items.summary: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a neurodegenerative tauopathy characterized by heterogeneous clinical presentations and disruption of distributed neural networks. Resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) provides a systems-level approach to examine intrinsic brain connectivity and may offer insights into disease-related network dysfunction. In this study, we compared rs-fMRI connectivity measures between individuals with PSP and healthy controls and explored differences across PSP clinical variants. 23 participants with probable or possible PSP and 23 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent structural and functional MRI. Graph theory metrics and functional connectivity measures across seven canonical resting-state networks were analyzed.…

items.title: Practical evaluation of AI models to forecast a respiratory seasonal epidemic in Canada
items.summary: Public health organizations can benefit greatly from infectious disease epidemic forecasting to guide and support interventions and policies that reduce morbidity. However, accurate and reliable epidemic forecasting remains notoriously challenging and is an evolving field in which new scientific advances continue to support forecasting efforts. Computational models that underpin artificial intelligence (AI) models are promising developments that may improve seasonal epidemic forecasting. This study aims to compare the performance of a selection of AI models previously identified as well adapted to epidemic forecasting, including machine learning (XGBoost), deep learning models (Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Transformer), time-series foundation model (Chronos), and a hybrid model: physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), against statistical models…

items.title: Deep learning of point-of-care lung ultrasound and clinical data for pulmonary tuberculosis triage in Uganda
items.summary: Rationale: Point of care lung ultrasound is portable and radiation free and could extend tuberculosis screening to settings without chest radiography, but no standardized criteria exist for interpreting it for tuberculosis. Objectives: To develop and internally evaluate deep learning models that classify pulmonary tuberculosis from lung ultrasound images, alone and combined with routine clinical variables, and to derive an abbreviated scanning protocol. Methods: In a prospective study in Kampala, Uganda (2023 to 2025), we enrolled people aged 13 years or older with microbiologically confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis, their household contacts, and symptomatic people with other respiratory conditions. One still frame from each of 12 lung ultrasound zones was analyzed with an attention-based multiple-instance learning network.…

items.title: Adversarial Robustness of Capsule Networks for Medical Image Classification
items.summary: Purpose: Deep learning models are increasingly being used in medical diagnostics, but their vulnerability to adversarial perturbations raises concerns about their reliability in clinical applications. Capsule networks (CapsNets) are a promising architecture for medical imaging tasks, given their ability to model spatial relationships and train with smaller amounts of data. Although previous studies have focused on adversarial training approaches to improve robustness, exploring alternative architectures is an underexplored direction for combating poor adversarial stability. Prior work has suggested that CapsNets may exhibit improved robustness to adversarial perturbations compared to convolutional neural networks (CNNs), but performance on adversarial images has not been studied systematically in clinical environments.…

items.title: High-resolution spatiotemporal estimates of total and wildfire PM2.5 in the contiguous United States, 2018-2024: Implications for population exposure and mortality burden
items.summary: Wildfire smoke has become an increasing public health concern in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Previous studies have provided high-resolution estimates of either total PM2.5 or wildfire-related PM2.5 during the past two decades, but few have focused on the most recent wildfire-intensive years, and jointly estimated both to quantify wildfire contributions to total PM2.5 exposure. This study developed a high-resolution machine learning framework to estimate daily 1-km concentrations of total and wildfire-related PM2.5 across the CONUS from 2018 to 2024. This framework incorporates chemical precursors and wildfire smoke density as predictors and relies on publicly accessible data sources enabling future updates. The model achieved high performance with cross-validated R2 of 0.72 and 0.89 for daily and annual estimates, respectively.…

items.title: Deep Time-to-Event Models for Intrapartum Fetal Monitoring
items.summary: Timely detection of fetal distress during labor is a central pursuit of modern obstetric care. The primary measure used in this regard is fetal heart rate and contraction monitoring (echocar-diotocography or CTG), which provides a continuous signal during labor. The vast majority of machine learning applications to CTG assume access to a 30 to 60 minute window just prior to delivery, which makes an untenable assumption that the timing of delivery is known. In this work, we reframe the problem as a time-to-event prediction task. We develop deep time-to-event models to predict the joint probability of imminent delivery and fetal acidosis, a biomarker of fetal hypoxia collected from umbilical cord gas after delivery.…

items.title: Human-Agentic AI Collaboration Workflow for Trend Analysis of ChatGPT Applications in Healthcare
items.summary: Background: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have demonstrated strong potential to transform healthcare research and practice. However, LLMs are probabilistic and generate inherently variable outputs, which create risk and uncertainty in healthcare applications. Therefore, analyzing the current research landscape of ChatGPT applications is imperative to understand applied techniques and related concerns and to facilitate their practical integration into healthcare information systems. Objective: Leveraging LLM-based agentic AI with domain experts to analyze trends in ChatGPT healthcare applications and to examine the collaborative and interpretative capacities of LLM agents in broader contexts beyond narrowly defined topics.…

items.title: Evaluation of System One Models on Biomedical Texts
items.summary: Objective To compare the performance and cost of System One models (SOMs) with general-purpose large language models (LLMs) on biomedical tasks and evaluate confidence-based routing. Materials and Methods We evaluated three SOMs and three LLMs across seven datasets and eight endpoints covering question answering, error detection, structured extraction, and clinical-note assessment. Outcomes included task-specific performance, recorded inference cost and latency, and confidence calibration. Calibration data determined routing schemes and confidence thresholds to evaluate test predictions, with cost-matched random referral as a comparator. Results Claude Opus 5.5 had the highest primary performance on all eight endpoints. The strongest SOM, Jev, had competitive performance with the evaluated LLMs and cost less than 1% of Opus on most datasets.…

items.title: Population-scale machine learning models estimate individual-level risk for acute respiratory infection
items.summary: Summary / Abstract BackgroundModels based on administrative population health records can help improve understanding of disease and hospitalisation risk. This understanding can support evidence-based population health policy and processes. Influenza and other acute respiratory diseases place a large, inequitable burden on the New Zealand population and health care resources. We have developed and evaluated such models using retrospective New Zealand hospitalisation records linked to other administrative data to estimate individual-level risk of hospitalisation due to acute respiratory infection. MethodsWe analysed linked annual records for approximately 4{middle dot}85-5{middle dot}36 million people in 2017-2024. Six machine learning algorithms and eight variable sets were assessed using five-fold cross-validation grouped by demographic profile.…

items.title: Whole-genome sequencing enables improved AML diagnostics and refines assessment of TP53 allelic state and complex karyotype
items.summary: Accurate genetic characterization is central to modern acute myeloid leukemia (AML) diagnostics, yet current standard-of-care (SoC) testing relies on multiple complementary assays. We compared paired tumor-normal whole-genome sequencing (WGS) with SoC diagnostics in a population-based cohort of 109 adult AML patients, assessing variant detection, disease classification according to ICC 2022 and WHO 2022, and risk stratification according to ELN 2022. WGS showed high concordance with SoC across variant classes. When considering all reported SoC variants together with high-confidence WGS variants as true positives, WGS showed equal to higher sensitivity than SoC for single-nucleotide variants and small insertions/deletions (97% vs 92%), structural variants (SVs; 100% vs 87%), and copy-number alterations (CNAs; 88.5% both).…

items.title: Patient, carer and clinical stakeholder views on using artificial intelligence and machine learning for the histopathological diagnosis of duodenal biopsies
items.summary: Objective: Biopsies are examined under the microscope by a pathologist, giving a diagnosis, which guides treatment and predicts prognosis. A shortage of pathologists and increasing workload leads to diagnostic delays, while for duodenal (small intestinal) biopsies, variable diagnostic concordance between pathologists limits accuracy. These challenges have motivated us to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated approach for the automated diagnosis of up to 80% of duodenal biopsies (i.e., most cases of the two most frequent diagnoses: coeliac disease and normal). We set out to understand patient, carer and stakeholder views regarding the adoption of such technology. Methods and Analysis: We conducted mixed-methods stakeholder engagement (February 2024 to June 2026).…

items.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
items.summary: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. We study how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding balance model capacity with computation, memory access, and execution overhead. Our pretraining infrastructure builds on MindSpore HyperParallel, combining topology-aware hybrid sharding, efficient distributed optimizer execution, and coordinated management of long-sequence workloads and activation memory. CPU affinity and core isolation further reduce host scheduling interference.…

items.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
items.summary: Standard neural architectures such as the Transformer were chosen because they train well with gradient descent and run fast on GPUs. In weight-space programming, a large language model (LLM) writes target weights by hand without gradient-based training, so those reasons no longer apply. Should we keep the Transformer? Given minimal guidance, ten labeled examples, and a sandbox, mainly on multiple-choice questions, we task three frontier LLMs with either generating the weights of a fixed architecture or designing the architecture themselves. When free to design, all three compile plain-text facts into a sparse table queried by a fixed procedure, reaching up to 54.4% test accuracy. An LLM-designed model achieves higher test accuracy than the most accurate released Transformer that the same LLM wrote while using about 1,800x fewer parameters.…
items.tldr: When large language models write neural network weights without gradient-based training, they tend to design sparse table or associative-memory models that outperform same-sized Transformers with far fewer parameters and faster GPU inference, though pretrained LLMs remain more accurate.

items.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
items.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality. We profile the inference pipeline of state-of-the-art models and find that operations often treated as fixed implementation details, such as VAE decoding and KV cache updates, in fact account for over half of end-to-end inference latency. We challenge the assumption that these components are indispensable and replace them with lightweight alternatives.…

items.title: GameRealm: Grounding Visual Learning in Interactive Games
items.summary: Visual foundation models are central to physical intelligence, yet their development remains constrained by fragmented training datasets, inconsistent annotation quality, and limited multimodal supervision. To address these challenges, we introduce GameRealm, a large-scale, richly annotated dataset that grounds visual observations in synchronized, game-native supervision. GameRealm encompasses over 120 million RGB frames and 1,000 hours of gameplay footage across all views. Beyond its unprecedented scale, GameRealm provides rich multimodal supervision, including metric depth, camera parameters, synchronized audio, control inputs, and 3D point trajectories. Its diversity further extends to flexible view configurations, spanning single-view, stereo, multi-view, and panoramic recordings.…
items.tldr: GameRealm is a large-scale multimodal gameplay dataset with synchronized depth, camera, audio, control, and 3D trajectory annotations that improves visual foundation models for generation and geometric learning.

items.title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) enables a single student to absorb the skills of several domain teachers by learning from its own generated responses. We present Multimodal Model Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation Reasoner (M3OPD-Reasoner), a fully open recipe for post-training vision-language models (VLMs) over three reasoning domains: image STEM, image perception, and video. We curate two datasets, M3OPD-SFT-1.35M for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and M3OPD-RL-193K for reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable rewards. On these data, we compare post-training recipes that start from Qwen3.5-9B: training one model on the mixed data of all domains (MixSFT and MixRL), and training one teacher per domain with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO), directly or after an SFT warm-up, and distilling the teachers into one student with MOPD.…

items.title: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
items.summary: Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots. We introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation. At the low level, we develop a multi-agent post-training framework that adapts a humanoid foundation tracking model to physically coupled interactions between humanoids, enabling coordinated decentralized control from local observations alone. At the high level, we train a vision-language planner and design a speech-based leader-follower coordination mechanism to synchronize decentralized execution without network communication.…
items.tldr: A decentralized framework enables teams of humanoids to coordinate whole-body loco-manipulation over long horizons using low-level multi-agent post-training and a high-level vision-language planner with speech-based leader-follower synchronization.

items.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
items.summary: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data.…
items.tldr: Capable frozen LLM agents can autonomously construct context-based self-learning algorithms from basic resources and a general goal, yielding text artifacts that transfer to new game and 3D navigation tasks.

items.title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback
items.summary: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification. Given a boundary-representation part, stock, and material, a locally hosted, mid-sized open model proposes operations and cutting parameters for indexed three-axis machining. A geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, and returns feedback for plan refinement. Setup planning accounts for what the available cutters can physically reach, rather than visibility alone.…

items.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. Given a monocular video and initial 2D TCP queries, the tracker directly recovers metric TCP poses in SE(3) and gripper states alongside scene geometry and camera parameters. The generator samples local features from the same 4D representation along the recovered TCP tracks, then combines them with robot observations and language instructions to predict future TCP states.…

items.title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
items.summary: π^4 is a unified foundation model for 4D scene perception. From diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations in the wild---a single image, an unordered collection, or a video sequence---it recovers dense geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, together with 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs. It couples a geometry branch with a geometry-conditioned motion branch, which predicts image-space correspondences that are lifted into 3D using reconstructed target-view geometry. Across diverse benchmarks, π^4 achieves the best overall average rank in geometry evaluation, alongside competitive performance in single- and multiview 2D/3D point tracking and moving-object segmentation. With a shared backbone, the full geometry-and-motion system contains approximately 0.5B parameters---less than half the size of most baselines.…
items.tldr: This unified foundation model enables the recovery of dense geometry, camera poses, and object tracking from diverse, uncalibrated observations in 4D scenes using a shared geometry and motion branch architecture.

items.title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
items.summary: Training coding agents for long-horizon tasks requires environments with verifiable feedback. Existing pipelines often follow a linear process that ends with validation, establishing usability but providing little guidance on improving training value. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) often requires model rollouts or model training followed by downstream evaluation, with costs and feedback delays amplified on long-horizon tasks. How can we use timely, reliable proxy signals to improve training value and synthesize environments at scale? We present RepoFactory, an automated pipeline that converts real repositories into verifiable environments where agents build complete projects from scratch given a language specification. Its Environment Evolution Loop optimizes a multiplicative objective combining validity, structural coupling, and implementation scope through proxy feedback.…
items.tldr: RepoFactory converts real repositories into verifiable coding environments and optimizes them via an Environment Evolution Loop using proxy feedback, enabling trained coding agents to achieve strong gains on long-horizon coding and agentic benchmarks.

items.title: FMT: Lossless Image Compression in a Fixed Number of Parallel Steps
items.summary: Learned lossless codecs make smaller files than common classical codecs, yet the images we archive and train on still use classical codecs. A main reason is time: a learned codec takes seconds to decode a photo that a classical codec opens in milliseconds, and their faster variants give up most of their gain in size. We argue that much of this time is spent waiting, not computing: the network waits for the values it conditions on, and the arithmetic decoder reads them one at a time. We introduce FMT (Fixed-step Multiscale Tree), a lossless image format whose decoding order and entropy coder are designed together so that neither wait grows with the image.…
items.tldr: The Fixed-step Multiscale Tree (FMT) format achieves highly efficient, fixed-time decoding of images by utilizing a coarse-to-fine tree structure and parallel GPU prediction mechanisms.

items.title: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference
items.summary: CAD practitioners often work with proprietary parts that they are unwilling to share with external services. For individuals and small companies, bringing this work in-house also requires computational resources they can afford. We introduce CADMAGEDDON, an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes and can run locally on single-GPU systems and current-generation laptops. The method decomposes this complex task into a chain of simple visual decisions about what to construct and what to correct. Geometric tools support precise construction, allowing the agent to focus on visual reasoning. Using the mid-sized Qwen3.8-27B model, CADMAGEDDON outperforms prior approaches, including systems based on frontier models, in reconstruction quality on all the main benchmarks.…
items.tldr: CADMAGEDDON is an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes locally on single-GPU systems and laptops, using a mid-sized Qwen model and geometric tools to outperform prior systems.

items.title: TPHC: Improving Hyper-Connections with Tensor-Parallel Grouped Updates
items.summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) expand the residual stream of a Transformer into N parallel streams, and manifold-constrained HC (mHC) stabilizes them at scale. However, mHC benefits little from more than four streams, partly because each sublayer writes a single output to all streams, limiting how differently they can be updated. In this work, we propose TPHC, which integrates tensor-parallel (TP) shards with HC streams to promote greater independence across streams. Specifically, we route a separate mixture of the residual streams to each TP shard and keep the individual shard outputs separate during write-back, so each stream can receive a different mixture of those outputs. This design makes the residual-stream updates more expressive without adding parameters or FLOPs to the attention or FFN sublayers.…
items.tldr: TPHC combines tensor-parallel shards with hyper-connection residual streams to enable more independent stream updates, improving language model loss and zero-shot reasoning with modest training overhead.

items.title: Attention at Absolute Zero
items.summary: Attention scores candidate supports of an answer, which we call witnesses, and reads the scores at a temperature. We build a higher-order attention layer whose state lives on pairs of items: for a pair (a, b), each third item k is a witness judged through its legs (a, k) and (k, b). It reads witnesses at zero temperature, keeping the best and the number tied with it, passes on only bits comparing such counts, rebuilds its pair state from the input and these bits at every loop, and is trained from answers alone. Each choice removes one way soft attention fails at size: dispersed weight, unresolved gaps between learned scores, and a drifting soft state. In maximum retrieval it is right on at least 99.95% of sets 1,000 times larger than in training, on all ten seeds; trained with a soft count, the same network falls to 42% at 4,096 items.…

items.title: CADD-SV v2.0: An Extended Framework for Structural Variant Deleteriousness Prediction Using Coordinate- and Sequence-Based Features
items.summary: Structural variants are a major source of genomic variation and contribute to human disease and evolution through diverse mechanisms, yet their functional interpretation remains challenging. We present CADD-SV v2.0, an improved machine learning framework for scoring SV deleteriousness that expands on the original CADD-SV implementation. This version introduces a unified Random Forest model trained on an expanded set of proxy-neutral and proxy-deleterious variants drawn from human and non-human primate genomes. The model integrates updated genomic annotations, including constraint metrics, regulatory elements, and chromatin architecture features. It scores Deletions, Insertions, Duplications and Inversions based on a single scoring framework that uses both the variant and its flanking regions.…

items.title: AlphaGenome 2 predicts regulatory activity and variant effects across cell states
items.summary: Most genetic variants associated with human traits and diseases lie in non-coding DNA, where they can alter gene regulation in specific cell types and states. Single-cell atlases chart these states across tissues and development, but rarely profile enough donors to associate variants with expression directly. Deep learning models could bridge this gap by predicting variant effects from DNA sequence, yet they poorly distinguish related cell states and require fine-tuning for new datasets. Here we present AlphaGenome 2 (AG2), which substantially advances cell-type-specific prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects for gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Trained on organism-wide human and mouse single-cell atlases and bulk functional genomics data, AG2 takes as input a 1-Mb DNA sequence and a condition specifying a target tissue, cell type, or cell state.…

items.title: MINA: Do frozen DNA encoders beat sequence composition? A homology-aware linear-probe benchmark
items.summary: Frozen DNA encoders are widely used as feature extractors, but fine-tuning hides what their fixed embeddings already make linearly accessible. MINA is a lightweight benchmark that asks whether those embeddings beat sequence composition, with two linear probes on 3,244 human genes: 5-way classification into coarse protein families, and regression onto each gene's GenePT text-summary embedding. Mostly, they do not. On coding sequence (CDS) under a homology aware split, the validation-selected encoder, NT-v2, recovers coarse family signal at about the level of nucleotide composition (macro-F1 0.693 vs. 0.639; Holm p = 0.108) but does not reach amino-acid composition (0.767) or the protein language model ESM-2 (0.954). On GenePT, DNABERT-2 beats nucleotide composition (R2 0.065 vs. 0.039) but not amino-acid composition (0.080).…

items.title: High-throughput prediction of peptide structural conformations
items.summary: Protein structure prediction via artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) approaches has sparked substantial research interest in structural biology. In recent work, AlphaFold2 (AF2) has been adapted for the prediction of multiple structural conformations, beyond static structures, by using multiple random seeds and subsampling the multiple sequence alignment (MSA). Research applying this specialized approach has focused on regular-sized proteins, while smaller peptides remain underexplored in this context. Here, we report AF2-based multi-conformation prediction and systematic analyses of a set of 557 peptides (10-40 residues in length) with corresponding nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) ensemble coordinates.…

items.title: AI-readiness criteria for biomedical data in functional genomics and clinical medicine
items.summary: Biomedical research is rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI). Yet the inherent complexity of biomedical data preparation requires implementing actionable, robust criteria for ethical and explainable AI (XAI) at the "pre-model" stage, encompassing data acquisition, detailed transformations, and ethical governance. Simple conformance to FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) Principles is insufficient. Here, we define criteria and practices for reliable AI-readiness of biomedical data, developed by the NIH Bridge to Artificial Intelligence (Bridge2AI) Standards Working Group across seven core dimensions of dataset AI-readiness: FAIRness, Provenance, Characterization, Ethics, Pre-model Explainability, Sustainability, and Computability.…

items.title: Constructing Gene Regulatory Network using Chatterjee's Rank Correlation with Single-cell Transcriptomic Data
items.summary: Constructing gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is critical for understanding cellular systems, yet existing methods rely either on strong modeling assumptions or on computationally intensive algorithms. We introduce a multiple testing framework for GRN construction based on Chatterjee's rank correlation coefficient, a nonparametric measure of dependence that captures non-linear and non-monotone relationships. The framework overcomes several limitations of traditional methods by offering a transparent, scalable, and computationally efficient alternative to recent black-box machine learning models. Because cells in scRNA-seq data are not independent observations, we develop a data-driven algorithm for estimating robust testing cutoffs.…

items.title: EvoRx: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Antibiotic Resistance in Escherichia coli Using Genomic Features
items.summary: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) complicates bacterial infection management, motivating genomic approaches to predicting antibiotic susceptibility. This study assessed the predictive performance and generalisability of machine-learning models using resistance-associated genomic features from Escherichia coli. Publicly available genomic and phenotypic records yielded 446 genomes, 252 binary genomic features and 1,935 susceptibility observations across nine antibiotics. Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers were compared using validation ROC-AUC, followed by evaluation on held-out test subsets. Additional analyses examined identical genomic feature profiles across partitions, performance across source publications and feature redundancy.…

items.title: Generalist method to reconstruct metabolic networks from multi-omics data at large-scale
items.summary: Metabolic network databases often suffer from inconsistent pathways with blocked reactions. Furthermore, current reconstruction methods lack scalable ways to integrate multi-omics data and cannot flexibly combine diverse modeling pipelines. We introduce SPECTRA, a unified platform that reconstructs metabolic networks across multiple biological scales. SPECTRA uses distinct optimization formulations and achieves a 56-fold speed improvement over existing algorithms for flux consistency based model reconstruction. We demonstrated SPECTRA across three applications. First, we gap-filled 7,302 microbial reconstructions from the AGORA2 database, reducing blocked reactions from an average of 482 to 169 per model. Second, we modeled synthetic gut microbiota at the community scale with superior performance in reaction inclusion.…

items.title: Multi-Model Comparison of Deep and Classical Architectures for ECG Diagnostic Superclass Classification on PTB-XL
items.summary: Objective. It remains unclear which architecture best sorts 12-lead electrocardiograms into diagnostic superclasses, and whether added model complexity pays off. Methods. Using 21,375 PTB-XL records under one patient-level split, we compared a Mamba-style state space model, a residual convolutional network, a bidirectional long short-term memory network, a convolutional-recurrent network with attention, soft-voting ensembles of these networks, and MiniRocket features with LightGBM. Each record took the superclass of its highest-likelihood diagnostic code, and we scored saved predictions with paired patient-level bootstrap intervals. Results. No model clearly outperformed MiniRocket with LightGBM, which needs no graphics processor.…

items.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
items.summary: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. Fortunately, an LLM agent can take over this design by refining the recipe over rounds of building and evaluating candidates, so that more rounds lead to better recipes. However, evaluating one quantized reasoning model takes tens of GPU-hours, and combining methods from different codebases means porting each to the new architecture by hand. We present QDA, a system in which an agent designs the recipe for each model and precision.…

items.title: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization
items.summary: Autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models predict discrete action tokens with the next-token objective of their vision-language backbone, so the action tokenizer defines the interface between the policy and the robot. In bimanual manipulation, the two arms share a repertoire of movements yet coordinate through complementary roles, and an action representation should capture both. However, most existing tokenizers encode both arms as a single concatenated action vector, in which motion patterns common to the two arms are not shared and cross-arm dependencies remain entangled within each token. The policy must therefore learn both aspects implicitly. We propose Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization (BiCAT), which shares one motion representation across arms while conditioning each arm's tokens on its partner through symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder.…
items.tldr: BiCAT shares a motion representation across arms and conditions each arm's tokens on its partner via symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder, enabling parallel arm token prediction and improving bimanual manipulation success.

items.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
items.summary: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few causal steps without accumulating drift across self-generated history. We present Invoker-Render, pairing a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language.…

items.title: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
items.summary: Language models can gain capacity at little computational cost from n-gram embedding tables: large tables of learned vectors for short sequences of consecutive tokens, which are looked up and added to the model's input or to its intermediate layers. Recent designs commonly use a separate n-gram embedding table for each layer, which makes the tables costly in memory and prevents layers from sharing what they learn. Sharing a single table, however, gives every layer the same embedding and leaves no room for layer-wise preferences, and it performs poorly in practice. We propose Chorus, in which one set of n-gram embedding tables serves the whole network and every layer reads it in its own way. Each layer maps the refined embedding through its own projection layer, after rescaling its components by factors computed from its current hidden state.…
items.tldr: Chorus shares one set of n-gram embedding tables across all layers, letting each layer project and rescale the embedding using its hidden state, achieving better quality with much smaller tables and lower optimizer memory.

items.title: NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding
items.summary: Fine-grained questions about long videos ask how many times an action occurs, in what order events unfold, or exactly when a state changes. Answering them can require finding brief moments scattered across hours of footage. Agentic models that decide when and where to look promise to find these moments, yet this ability is hard both to measure and to learn. Sparse supporting evidence may establish that an action occurred without establishing its total count; verifying timeline-wide claims requires checking for missed occurrences and double counting. Answer-only supervision, in turn, does not explicitly supervise the search for evidence. We present NexSight, which builds verifiable tasks to both evaluate and train agentic long-video understanding.…

items.title: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs
items.summary: The goal of this paper is to reduce the input token cost of Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) at inference time. Omni-LLMs reason jointly over audio, video and text, but the cost of the three streams is highly unbalanced: visual tokens account for the vast majority of the input, and are highly redundant. In this paper, we propose ReMo, a training-free framework that compresses visual tokens by redistributing their information across modalities: a visual token is kept only if its information appears nowhere else. ReMo achieves this in two ways: (i) it aligns audio and video in a shared space via closed-form calibration, and removes visual tokens already explained by the audio or by other visual tokens; and (ii) it replaces object-level visual tokens, identified by a lightweight object detector, with compact text proxies, short descriptions of each object and its location,…
items.tldr: ReMo, a training-free method, reduces inference input token cost for omni-modal large language models by compressing redundant visual tokens through cross-modal alignment and replacing object-level visual tokens with compact text descriptions, achieving comparable accuracy on audio-visual tasks.

items.title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations
items.summary: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change.…

items.title: DiagTrace: An Interactive Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on medical question answering and diagnostic reasoning benchmarks. However, existing evaluations typically provide all patient information upfront and assess only the final diagnosis or rationale. This setup ignores the need to acquire diagnostic evidence incrementally from incomplete information in real-world diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we introduce DiagTrace, a source-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can reconstruct the documented diagnostic trajectory through interactive information seeking. Each benchmark instance is built from a PubMed Central case report and includes an initial presentation, an event bank, a clinical course, and diagnostic references. DiagTrace contains 510 cases across eight specialties, with 225 used to evaluate four LLMs on clinical-course alignment, interaction quality, and efficiency.…

items.title: Stokes flow in a wedge with a moving contact point: well-posedness with a fixed contact angle and Navier slip
items.summary: We study 2D Stokes flow in a wedge-like region bounded by a solid substrate with Navier slip and by a free surface driven by surface tension. The two meet at a moving contact point with a fixed contact angle. This is the model of a moving contact line at scales below the slip length, in its simplest setting. The slip length is the only length scale, and nothing is prescribed at the contact point beyond the angle: no relaxation law for the angle, and no contact-point dissipation. Slip removes the paradox found by Huh and Scriven, the infinite dissipation at a contact line that moves without slip, but in this model a weaker singularity remains. We give, to our knowledge, the first rigorous characterisation of this singularity for solutions of the free-boundary problem near the stationary state.…

items.title: DreamFAR: Real-Time and Long-Horizon Interaction with Diverse Objects
items.summary: World models have shown great potential in serving as a simulator for robot manipulation. However, existing models are either fit to a single environment or lack ability to simulate long-horizon contact-rich events. We present DreamFAR, a world model whose dynamics model is trained from scratch on a large robot-native teleoperation dataset, with no internet-video pretraining. We present an architecture and learning recipe designed for training on robot-native data. DreamFAR is significantly smaller than the high-performance video generation models, yet shows better understanding of contact and causality, and runs 10 FPS on a commercial GPU. Experimentally, DreamFAR significantly outperforms existing models in predicting the long-horizon future. We further demonstrate various applications where DreamFAR can be used, including policy evaluation and mixed-data co-training.…

items.title: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
items.summary: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. We specify the design: storage record, budget-derived retention, append-only read path, and bounded aggregation.…

items.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Hard Constraints: Policy Gradient Methods with Intersample Guarantees
items.summary: We develop a policy-gradient (PG) reinforcement learning (RL) framework with hard inter-sample control barrier function (CBF)-based safety constraints for nonlinear sampled-data systems. We first design a class of stochastic policies with support truncated to sampling-period-dependent safe control sets, that guarantee safety-by-construction at sampling instants. We then propose a model-free PG algorithm that searches over the class of safe-by-design policies and establish sufficient conditions on sampling-period such that any action sampled from safe control sets remains safe throughout the sampling interval, providing inter-sample guarantees. We further establish finite-time convergence and sample complexity guarantees for the proposed PG algorithm and characterize its global optimality under gradient dominance.…

items.title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
items.summary: Language models are dynamical systems. A transformer is iterated over its layers, over the steps of its training and over the tokens it generates, and on each of these three clocks it shows behavior that nonlinear dynamics has studied for a century: fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, chaos and noise-driven escape from potential wells. The two communities rarely meet, so this behavior is often rediscovered under new names. We build a bridge between them. To describe, we condense about 200 papers into the Three-Clock Dictionary, which maps fifteen concepts of nonlinear dynamics onto each clock and marks every correspondence as proved, measured or conjectured, and we show each concept in a mechanical system and in a language model side by side.…

items.title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
items.summary: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and budgets, while hosts distribute the public program and may retain private services server-side.…

items.title: Pathology Randomization for Synthetic Priors and Zero-Shot Detection
items.summary: Hospital brain imaging archives hold a diverse array of pathology at sample sizes beyond prospective studies, particularly for underrepresented populations and diseases. To unlock uncurated clinical data and scale analysis, methods are needed to detect abnormalities across contrasts and resolutions. Synthetic data has provided robust, contrast-agnostic models for a variety of human neuroimaging tasks in healthy anatomy, but pathology detection and other tasks in clinical settings still require real patient data, contrast-specific models, or disease-specific generators. We propose PathoDraw, a generative model of brain MRI with pathology. A conditional distribution of lesions given the healthy anatomy is drawn into the label map before contrast-agnostic rendering, and a single network estimates healthy anatomy with exact signed intensity deviation of any input scan.…

items.title: Solver to System: LLM Reasoning Across Representations and Execution in Scientific Simulation
items.summary: Simulators based on partial differential equations (PDEs) are widely used to model physical systems, but generating and interpreting PDE solver code with large language models (LLMs) remains challenging. Scientific simulation code is a useful testbed for LLM scientific reasoning because (1) one system can be represented by code, equations, natural language, and numerical trajectories and (2) code can execute successfully while implementing invalid physics. We introduce Solver2System, a dataset of PDE solvers with multiple representations, controlled corruptions, and lexical perturbations, to evaluate whether LLMs can recover the underlying physical system through (1) cross-representation consistency and (2) static and agentic detection of physical invalidity.…

items.title: OCCAM: Improved Single-Cell Representation Learning and Perturbation Effect Prediction
items.summary: Predicting the effects of genetic perturbations requires models that generalize beyond observed cell contexts and gene combinations. We introduce Occam, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) framework for representation learning and perturbation-effect prediction. Occam combines cell representations learned through denoising with gene interaction, text, and protein-sequence features. It achieves the highest aggregate representation scores for perturbation information and cell-type preservation with batch integration. In cross-context few-shot prediction, a perturbation and a cell context are each observed during training, but never together. Occam better captures the measured response patterns for these unobserved combinations than four retrained competitors or direct transfer of the same perturbation's measured effects from other training cell lines.…

items.title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
items.summary: Weight-space programming is a process where a large language model reads and writes the weights of a neural network directly, guided by a natural language specification, without an optimiser or gradient descent. This study applies it to automatic tractor guidance, where a 253-parameter neural network steers along paths of lines and arcs and must be adapted when the machine changes, such as a slower steering actuator. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (also 5.2) edited the network for our research tractor using a small budget of simulated evaluations to repair a network trained for another tractor and write a controller into a network with zero weights. We compared them with an evolution strategy, gradient descent and pure pursuit in simulation and on the real tractor.…

items.title: SCAN: Site-Aware Collaborative Privacy-Preserving Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for Neurological Disease Classification
items.summary: Worldwide neuroimaging data could strengthen diagnostic foundation models, but privacy rules often prevent centralizing brain MRI scans. We present SCAN, a site-aware collaborative adaptation framework for Neurological Disease Classification that lets new sites adapt a 3D medical vision-language model (VLM) without retraining or sharing patient scans. Each site keeps exact class prototypes for local prediction and can share privacy-protected class summaries: norm-bounded sums and counts perturbed once with calibrated noise. Using 7,641 scans from 67 sites across 12 countries, covering Alzheimer's disease (AD), stroke, epilepsy and controls, we assess local adaptation, cross-site benefits, and effects on existing sites. At seven unseen sites, the frozen VLM's zero-shot AUCs were 0.833-0.945 for AD and stroke.…

items.title: doctolib-lab/doctosae-medembed-large-v0.1
items.summary: feature-extraction / pytorch

items.title: Complexity and precision in quantum associative retrieval
items.summary: We show that efficient and high-precision quantum associative retrieval is possible with an exponential complexity advantage with respect to the classical brute force approach and with a polynomial capacity advantage with respect to classical neural network implementations for any number of patterns scaling polynomially in the number of qubits. Both classical neural and quantum associative memories store the patterns in a Hamiltonian; in the classical case the dynamics is irreversible relaxation toward attractors, in the quantum case it is unitary transformations generating an effective thermal distribution, followed by a measurement.

items.title: Does the Model Use What It Cites? Counterfactual Tests of Grounded Reasoning Chains in Small Video-Language Models
items.summary: A grounded reasoning chain cites a frame span and a box for every step, so a reader can check where the model looked. Whether the answer depends on the cited region is a different question. We test it by intervention: the regions a model cited in its own chain are blacked out, and the share of correct answers that flip is compared with blacking out boxes of the same size elsewhere on the same frames. The paired difference, the cite gap, needs no annotation. We apply it to 2-3B video-language models trained on exact CLEVRER chains and on pseudo-labelled NExT-QA chains.
